notes: On 29 September 2022, police agents and firefighters from the Professional Union of Local Police and Firefighters (SPPLB) held a rally in Town Hall square in Valencia (Valencia) to protest delays in updating payroll, overtime work and the alleged lack of compliance with the agreements adopted in terms of personnel by the municipal government.

On 3 November 2023, at the call of UIL UILTUCS, Karibu and Aid consortium workers gathered outside the courthouse in Buozzi square in Latina (Latina, Lazio) to protest against the lack of oversight of project providers who did not notice that tax crimes were being committed and that false invoices were being issued by at least six people working in a cooperative managing asylum seekers and unaccompanied minors in the province of Latina.
On 12 January 2025, over 100 border police officers protested in Sculeni, against pay cuts for weekend and public holiday working hours.

On 24 April 2026, members and supporters of the National Alternative Movement organized a flash mob titled 'Corridor of Shame' in front of the Parliament building in Chisinau - Centru (Centru, Chisinau) against rising fuel prices and the administrative-territorial reform law on the amalgamation of localities, carrying banners reading 'PAS is destroying town halls', 'People pay the crisis, PAS comments on it', and 'At the pump it is dire, from PAS no movement'.

On 3 February 2025, at 3:30 pm, at the call of the Beziers-Herault tobacconists' federation, around 20 people, including national deputy Julien Gabarron (RN) and Mayor Robert Menard (Independent), staged a protest in front of the Flash tobacco shop in Beziers (Occitanie) against the sale of contraband cigarettes and tobacco.
On 19 April 2024, students' parents and local elected officials demonstrated in Bernaville (Hauts-de-France) to protest against the closure of classes at the local school.

On 21 July 2021, about 30 anarchist activists gathered outside Palazzo Ducale in Genova (Genova, Liguria) to protest against the participation of a magistrate and a police union representative in a conference organized by Amnesty International for the 20th anniversary of the July 2001 G8 summit and the anti-globalization demonstration recorded on that occasion. Protesters denounced a 'complacent' judiciary and 'murderous' police, notably in relation to the death of an anti-globalization activist in 2001.
On 30 May 2021, residents of the Gorublyane district in Sofia organized a protest and demanded compensation for forced expropriation.

On 28 November 2020, several hundred people, including union members and LDH activists, demonstrated in Nancy against a national security bill that they condemned as a violation of freedom of information, protesters' rights, and media rights, as well as the implementation of global surveillance of citizens.
On 17 February 2024, over 1,000 people, including health workers, gathered in Lannion (Bretagne) to protest against the closure of the local hospital's emergency unit at night.
On 26 February 2022, at the call of the CGT, health workers at EHPAD centre demonstrated in Grainville-sur-Oron to denounce the lack of resources.

On 19 May 2026, residents, activists, MPs Laura Boldrini (PD), Marianna Madia (IV), Stefania Ascari (M5S), Senators Valeria Valente (PD), Cecilia D'Elia (PD), Ilaria Cucchi (SI), municipal councilors elected with the PD, the M5S, and FdI gathered in the Campidoglio Square in Roma - City Center (Lazio) to protest the forced removal, ordered by the Juvenile Court, of a minor who was subsequently entrusted to her father, who was indicted for aggravated assault. Protesters demanded that the child be reunited with her mother instead.
Around 12 September 2022 (as reported), students of the Nimes Conservatory gathered for a protest in front of the theater in Nimes, to demand more study spaces and rooms.

On 8 January 2025, tens of policemen protested in front of Police Station Four in Cluj-Napoca against the 'little train' ordinance. Officers argued that the ordinance removes additional pay for work performed on weekends and public holidays, resulting in income reductions of up to 2,000 lei in some cases, particularly for those with many years of service.

On 2 July 2020, prison police staged a protest in Rome - City Center (Roma, Lazio) to demand urgent measures to support the prison system that is about to collapse and support prison police activities. Protesters gathered at the call of the Union of Prison Police Unions.
On 11 October 2025, SNS supporters gathered in Mokrin to march in support of Serbs in Kosovo, backing the government and opposing student-led protests and blockades.

On 9 December 2024, about 300 students from the Bergese Rosselli Institute protested in Sestri Ponente (Liguria) against inadequate heating in classrooms, restrictions on student movement, and disruptions caused by a nearby construction site affecting the entire school. They raised concerns about cold classrooms, collective punishment for smoking violations, safety issues such as collapsing ceilings and lack of bathroom doors, and noise from ongoing renovations, arguing it sometimes disrupted lessons.

On 26 October 2024, at the call of Europe for Peace, Italian Network for Peace and Disarmament and local associations, around 5,000 people marched from Massari Square to Prefettura Square in Bari (Puglia) to advocate for peace and a ceasefire in all conflicts. CGIL, ANPI, students, SI, AVS, M5S, a city councilor (PD) and other associations took part in the event.

On 27 September 2022, around 60 Groupama workers, including Christians, gathered in front of the site of the company in Pau at the call of CFDT, CFE CGC, SNEEMA, CGT, FO, CFTC, and UNSA, calling for an increase in their salaries to face the inflation.

On 16 January 2021, a handful of parents of students gathered in La Roche-sur-Yon. They denounced the bill on the reinforcement of laicity according to which school will become compulsory from the age of three until the age of sixteen, and home-schooling will no longer be permitted by 2021.
On 3 March 2023, parents gathered in Am Mellensee to symbolically hand over their claims to the school administration, protesting against the planned closure of a kindergarten in the town.

On 29 September 2022, demonstrators, including members of the Swedish-Iranian community, demonstrated in Stockholm to show support and solidarity with Iranian protesters and to denounce the death of a 22-year-old Kurdish woman in police custody in Iran. Activists from the Socialist Justice Party took part in the event, among others.

On 21 March 2022, over 200 people gathered in Pieve di Cadore (Belluno, Veneto) at the call of Libera on the occasion of the 'Day of remembrance and commitment in memory of the innocent victims of mafias'. They demonstrated against organized crime. Students and the Prefect took part in the demonstration.

On 16 October 2021, around 20 members of the Yellow Vests movement gathered at a roundabout and slowed traffic down in La Roche-sur-Yon. They denounced the rise of gas prices, as part of a national day of protests.
On 18 August 2023, Rehabilitation Institute workers blocked the road in Igalo, protesting against the Institute's bankruptcy and losing their jobs.

Around 1 February 2026 (as reported), supporters, anti-racist activists, and relatives gathered in Dunkerque (Hauts-de-France) to protest in support of the family of Djamel Bendjaballah, murdered by his wife's former partner. Protesters denounced what they describe as a racist, premeditated killing, and condemned the justice system's refusal to recognize the racist motive and prior institutional failures.

On 16 November 2024, residents of the Kisela Voda neighborhood in Skopje came out for a peaceful protest at the intersection between Narodni Heroi and Boris Trajkovski streets due to unresolved infrastructure problems and legal violations by the surrounding construction sites, which, according to the residents, significantly threaten the safety of pedestrians make it difficult for them to access their homes.

On 24 February 2024, several hundred people staged a protest in Neubrandenburg (Mecklenburg-Vorpommern) against right-wing extremism and xenophobia. Bundesrat President Manuela Schwesig (SPD) started the event with a speech. The protest was organized following reports about a secret meeting between AfD members and far-right activists in Potsdam in November 2023, during which remigration plans were discussed.

On 16 February 2020, several hundred people, mostly Romani Hungarians, protested in Miskolc of the Borsod-Abauj-Zemplen county against the depicting of Roma people as criminals by far-right groups. The Miskolc branch of the Romani Self-Government organized the protest.
Around 12 October 2022 (as reported), at the call of USB, people gathered outside the town hall in Taranto (Taranto, Puglia) to protest against the increase in energy prices.

On 19 December 2021, several hundred activists gathered for a rally in Tarnow, protesting against a new law on media ownership, which they perceive as a harmful pressure of the government against independent media.
On 19 September 2021, citizens protested in Ourense (Galicia) against electricity price increases. The CIG trade union called the protest.

On 3 January 2026, around 100 people, including members of the local civil society group France-South America Association (Association France-Amerique Latine - AFAL) and Chilean nationals, spontaneously gathered at Place du Marche in Poitiers (Nouvelle-Aquitaine) to denounce the military intervention the United States conducted in Venezuela. The event was part of a wider national mobilization opposing US military intervention in Venezuela, which resulted in the abduction of President Nicolas Maduro and his wife on 3 January 2026, and aimed to demonstrate solidarity with the civilian population.

On 17 May 2025, over 200 people, including Senegalese relatives, gathered in Rimini (Emilia-Romagna) to demand the immediate release of Louis Dassilva, a Senegalese man under investigation for the July 2024 murder of Pierina Paganelli. Demonstrators marched through the city center holding banners and flyers. Participants called for justice and questioned the grounds for his continued detention.
On 15 June 2020, Kurdish protesters from NCDK demonstrated outside the European Commission office in Helsinki, protesting against Turkey's recent bombings in northern Iraq.
On 15 June 2022, several drivers protested at an OMV petrol station in Sibiu, condemning the high fuel prices and intentionally slowing access to the station.
On 9 January 2020, highschool students staged a protest outside their school's main building in Salerno (Salerno, Campania) to complain about the building's infrastructural problems.
On 11 June 2021, employees of a shipyard protested outside the economy ministry in Bucharest, condemning the announced firing of more than 200 employees.

On 14 August 2021, around 100 Extinction Rebellion activists staged a street blockade in central Tampere, demanding climate action. Police asked protesters to leave and moved them away by force. 38 people were detained for not following orders.

On Apr. 20, 2018: Citizens and members of the opposition democrat party threw smoke grenades and fireworks at the Shkodra's Appeal Court in Shkoder, demanding the release of the 11 demonstrators arrested for the Nation's Road riot.

On 17 June 2024, at the call of ELA, LAB, CCOO and National Police Union (Sindicato Abertzale de la Ertzaintza, ESAN), Independent Union of the Basque Police (Euskal Poliziaren sindikatu independentea, ERNE), around 200 municipal police officers protested in Bilbao (Pais Vasco) against planned municipal cuts to their vacations and release schedules.

On 16 August 2022, Extinction Rebellion activists staged a protest performance in front of the Swedish Transport Administration office in Solna to oppose the current development policy of the government agency, arguing that they contribute to the climate crisis.
On 31 March 2018, 2018 in Banja Luka, Bosnia and Herzegovina, approximately 200 citizens held protest against unresolved death of youngster David Dragicevic.

On 30 August 2023, over 80 people, mostly members of Last Generation, demonstrated and slowed traffic down from the Isartor to the Bavarian State Parliament in Munchen (Bayern) to call for climate protection. 11 sat down on the street and were carried away by police officers. Around 10 people threw paintballs at the building of the Bavarian State Parliament.
On 7 October 2023, activists, including members of the Women's Strike movement, gathered for a rally in Krakow, calling for more women's' participation in politics and the public life.

On 29 July 2022, road construction workers protested in Veliko Tarnovo, blocking the Ruse-Svilengrad road, as they demand that their unpaid salaries for completed construction work be paid. Three-day protests have been organized nationwide and the protesters have announced a wider blockade of the road system in the upcoming months.
On 13 May 2023, 4 activists peacefully protested at the zoo in Duisburg against dolphin exploitation and abuse.
On 9 September 2024, students' parents blocked access to the Georges-Brassens school in Nezignan-l'Eveque (Occitanie) to protest against the announced closure of a class.

On 10 February 2021, a few hundred parents of students, accompanied by their children, but also grandparents, residents, and elected officials and elected officials protested in Neussargues en Pinatelle against the elimination of a job position at the school.
On 21 January 2026, people demonstrated in Oslo to protest an offensive led by the Syrian military against Kurdish-held areas, and to express solidarity with Rojava and Kurdish civilians.

On 19 July 2025, several hundred people staged a protest, marching from the central station to the Imam-Ali-Mosque, also known as the Blue Mosque, in Hamburg - Hamburg-Nord (Hamburg) demanding its reopening, which had been closed by federal authorities in 2024. Meanwhile, people gathered in two small counter-protests near the Imam-Ali-Mosque, opposing its reopening due to the mosque's ties to the Islamic Centre Hamburg, which had been banned for promoting the ideology of Iran's Islamic Revolution.

On 11 February 2021, 150 Air Italy former employees affiliated with COBAS, Associazione Piloti, USB and ANPAV took part in a sit-in outside the former Air Italy headquarters in Olbia (Sassari, Sardegna) to demand public authorities to acknowledge their collective fate and to ensure the renewal of the redundancy fund for most of the employees.
On 14 January 2022, workers at cash-in-transit company Loomis burned wooden pallets in front of the siege in Talaudiere area in Saint-Etienne to demand an increase to their salaries.

On 7 March 2025, around 80 people, including LFI, LE, and Pd! affiliates and students, gathered outside the Espace Dewailly in Amiens (Hauts-de-France) to protest against the launch of the RN municipal campaign in town.

On 12 September 2023, UGT members held a protest at the doors of their headquarters in Zaragoza (Zaragoza) to denounce the rise in fatal workplace accidents, which is 21 people since the beginning of the year.

On 25 March 2023, Extinction Rebellion activists gathered at the Salztorbrucke in Vienna - Inner City, to color part of the river green and block the bridge to protest against a gas conference taking place in Vienna.

On 20 June 2020, an unknown number of workers staged a protest at the Colruyt supermarket in Chenee in the context of a strike against the lack of reciprocity from the management for the efforts by the personnel to ensure maximum safety in the supermarkets.

Around 12 December 2022 (as reported), around 150 police officers staged a protest outside the city hall in Kortrijk to denounce the Federal Minister of Justice's failure to comply with a protocol that was agreed upon between the government and the police unions. Kortrijk is the residence city of the Minister.
On 8 February 2023, DK members, including a DK local councilor, protested outside a building where the Orban government held a session in Sopron against the sale of local government property.
On 16 July 2021, 15 people gathered in Muhldorf am Inn at a vaccination center trying to prevent parents with their children to get their children vaccinated.

On 6 June 2020, the Workers' Communist Party and the Front of the Communist Youth demonstrated in Rome - City Center (Roma, Lazio) to ask an extension of the current ban on redundancies and the establishment of an extraordinary asset tax. Around 1000 people participated. Media reported that the same protest occurred in 15 Italian cities.

On 13 July 2021, people gathered outside the Umbria Region Council headquarters in Perugia to protest against the financial cuts to local public transport. Filt CGIL, CISL, and Faisa CISAL took part in the demonstration.
On 13 October 2020, around 30 workers staged a protest in front of the Megaworld facility in Genk to demand more clarity on the store chain's survival.
On 1 October 2021, citizens called by the Committees for the Defence of the Republic (CDR) gathered in Tarragona (Catalonia) to commemorate the Catalan independence referendum held in 2017.

On 23 January 2026, former employees of US companies working in Iraq and Afghanistan protested in front of the public revenue office in Kumanovo. They demanded recognition of tax documents, an end to double taxation, and fair treatment under the law.

On 18 October 2022, around 1,000 people, including Yellow Vests, held a protest in Nancy against the reform of professional high schools, inflation, and called for the reevaluation of salaries and a better distribution of wealth. The event was part of a national and cross-sector day of strike and protest called by the CGT, FO, SUD, and FSU unions, as well as the FIDL, MNL, UNEF, and High School Voice student organizations, to demand salary increases amid inflation and defend the right to strike.

On 12 May 2023, at the call of Agerola Forum, people protested during the Giro d'Italia in Ravello (Salerno, Campania) to ask for more safety and road maintenance work. Some weeks before, a 29-year-old boy Nicola Fusco fell into an embankment while driving a tourist bus. Demonstrators showed their backs to the cyclists as a sign of protest.

On 14 February 2021, anti-fur demonstrators gathered in Bordeaux at the call of One Voice. They called for the closing of the seven remaining fur farms in France and the abolition of the production and exportation of fur.
On 20 December 2022, around 20 people, at the call of IL, demonstrated in front of the main station in Hamburg - Hamburg-Mitte (Hamburg) against controls (checks) of public transport tickets.
On 9 November 2020, hundreds of students from Lieto school marched from their school to the town hall in Lieto in protest against poor air quality at the school.
On 23 February 2022, striking haulers gathered for a protest in Palermo (Palermo, Sicilia). They denounced the increase in oil and gas prices.

On 18 March 2022, fishers demonstrated at the port of Les Sables-d'Olonne. They denounced the raise in the gas price and the consequences on their profession and demanded that the government grants them an increased allowance to compensate this raise.

On 27 October 2021, around 150 workers and union activists from 3F and BJMF unions, held a blockade of a construction site in Carlsberg, Copenhagen to oppose the German contractor who fired 21 carpenters. Union activists accused the contractor of social dumping and violating the collective bargaining agreement.

On 29 January 2022, hundreds of citizens protested in Barakaldo against the courts' decision to release a 53-year-old man responsible for an attack against a woman working in her bar. The judge decided to release the attacker after a medical report stated that he had a psychotic break.

On 1 May 2021, around 800 persons, including members of the SNES-FSU union, demonstrated in Carmaux at the call of the CGT and FSU unions on the occasion of Labour Day. They called for social justice.

On 22 May 2021, around 2000 interim civil servants protested in Madrid - Salamanca (Madrid), marching from Paseo del Prado towards Plaza de Colon to complain about the overuse of temporary contracts by public institutions. The protest was called nationwide by the Platform of Temporary Public Workers in Fraud of Law (MI15F) under the slogan 'Fijeza ya' (Fixity Now).

On 6 January 2025, around fifteen activists from Extinction Rebellion Achterhoek, joined by participants from Nijmegen, held a peaceful 'die-in' demonstration on Simonsplein in Doetinchem (Gelderland), during the monthly air-raid siren, to raise awareness about rising sea levels and the climate crisis.

On 8 May 2021, around 19 members of The Right protested in Einbeck with the slogan 'Against a Guilt Cult - Investigation Instead of Repentance' against Germany's 'guilt culture' with respect to its role in the Second World War. Around 17 people gathered spontaneously for a counterprotest.

On 27 December 2022, around 200 people, including members of the Kurdish community, demonstrated in Lille to denounce the killing of 3 Kurdish people in Paris on 23 December by a 69-year-old man with racist motives and the recent aggression of a Kurdish hairdresser in Roubaix.

On 27 January 2024, people took part in a protest in Siegen (Nordrhein-Westfalen) against right-wing extremism. The protest was prompted by concerns over a secret meeting between AfD representatives and other far-right activists, discussing mass deportations of individuals with German citizenship and migrant background, leading to a heightened awareness and mobilization against far-right ideas in various cities.
On 1 April 2022, Fridays for Future activists protested in Budapest - V, demanding climate action.

On 26 January 2025, following leaked cell phone calls of the last moments of the victims of the Tempe rail disaster, protesters rallied in Chios at the call of the association of the victims' families. The protesters demanded justice and accused the government of a cover-up. This was part of a large mobilization in more than 150 nationwide and international locations with the slogan 'I Have No Oxygen', the last words of one of the victims.

On 3 April 2022, hundreds of people and retirees, called by the O Novo Normal digital community, held a protest at the Pontevedra square of A Coruna (Galicia), to decry the banking sector's treatment of customers, specifically older people, who claimed to be excluded. Protesters also decried what they considered abusive fees and charges. The protest was supported by the BNG.
Around 25 July 2021, around 450 people, including school students, protested in Oberfahlheim against the closure of the local primary school.

On 28 July 2020, eleven 'Industrie Meccaniche Siciliane' workers gathered outside the Town Hall in Priolo Gargallo (Siracusa, Sicilia) to protest against a court's verdict that doesn't recognize them the rights and benefits after being exposed to asbestos. They started the protest on 6 July 2020, and they have been gathering outside the Town Hall every day since then.

On 5 June 2020, around 100 people, including a group of Brothers of Italy members, staged a protest in Siculiana (Agrigento, Sicily) to demand the closure of a migrant reception center located in their town.

On 14 September 2023, members of the Federation of Parents' Associations of Central Macedonia rallied outside the Ministry of Macedonia and Thrace in Thessaloniki to protest over safety issues regarding the transport of their children to school.

On 8 March 2025, at the call of UdU and High School Students' Network, people, including students, gathered in Venezia (Veneto) to protest neo-fascism, hate and homophobic crimes and intimidation after homophobic slurs and pro-fascist writings were painted on the doors of the two student associations' seats in the city. Representatives of ANPI, CGIL, 'Group 25 April' (Gruppo 25 Aprile), 'All the City Together' (Tutta la citta insieme), ADI, PD, M5S, city councilors, researchers, and members of self-managed social centers participated in the demonstration.

On 12 March 2024, around 100 workers and trade unions blocked the entrance to the construction site in Nordhavn, Copenhagen, accusing the owner of social dumping and breaching the collective agreement. The police later intervened and dispersed the activists.

On 29 January 2025, dozens of taxi drivers, called by Taxi National Association (Antaxi-Asociacion Nacional del Taxi), held a protest outside the Government Sub-delegation in Oviedo (Asturias) against skyrocketing insurance costs and demanded government intervention to cap policy hikes and ensure the sector's survival amid rising expenses.

On 14 March 2022, relatives and police unions gathered in Pozzuoli (Napoli, Campania) to commemorate two police officers who were shot dead in 2019. They demanded truth and justice for the police officers. SIAP took part in the demonstration.
On 1 January 2022, No Tav activists gathered outside the Turin-Lyon high-speed railway construction site in San Didero (Torino, Piemonte) to protest against the project.

On 22 October 2022, between 2,300 (according to the police) and 4,000 (according to organizers) people, at the call of unions (DGB, Ver.di), demonstrated in Dusseldorf under the slogan 'Solidarity through the crisis' to denounce inflation and its consequences. Demonstrators called for social justice (redistribution), and solidarity amid the energy crisis. 'Solidarity Autumn' (SH), the Parity Welfare Association (PW) called for the protest.

On 15 May 2021, Miliardo Yida Srl plastic and waste paper recovery workers staged a picket outside their company's gates in Pontecurone (Alessandria, Piemonte) to protest against allegedly unjustified layoffs.

On 24 January 2026, around 500 to 600 demonstrators, including Kurdish community members, gathered in Malmo, Skane, to protest a new offensive led by the Syrian military against Kurdish-held areas, and to express solidarity with Rojava and Kurdish civilians.
On 12 March 2022, around 30 truck drivers slowed down traffic between Steenvoorde and Lille to denounce increased fuel prices.

On 6 October 2025, citizens, including members of the SRCE and the citizen group 'Truth and Honor' ('Istina i cast'), organized by local opposition, held a protest in Cacak calling for unity among opposition parties and demanding extraordinary elections.
On 30 October 2021, local residents protested in Gornji Kosinj, Croatia against construction of a hydro power plant at the site of a cemetery.

On 9 May 2022, people, including students, the Vice Mayor, and a council member, gathered in Municipio Square in Napoli to mark Europe Day and call for peace. The Europe Direct office organized the demonstration.

On 23 January 2022, Pakistani students in Northern Cyprus rallied for hours at the scene of a traffic accident in Cengizkoy (Peristeronas), where a friend of theirs had just lost his life, and protested over the bad condition of the road and the late arrival of the funeral vehicle. The protesters attempted to block the road twice, but were not allowed, and after the body of their friend was driven away from the scene, they marched to Gemikonagi (Karavostasi) in protest.

On 15 July 2024, striking workers of National Advocacy Service (NAS) represented by SIPTU picketed outside their workplace in Monaghan (Monaghan) over a pay dispute. The event was part of a national industrial action. NAS workers support adults with disabilities across Ireland.

On 16 January 2021, between 200 and 250 persons demonstrated in Angouleme. They called for the removal of several articles of the 'comprehensive security' bill. Articles concerned were article 22 on the use of drones by the police, article 21 on the right for police or military officers to film on private device and share, when necessary, recordings of their operations, and article 24 that criminalizes disseminating images with personal identifiers of a police or military officer, with the aim of affecting his or her physical or psychological integrity.
On 15 December 2024, residents of Gaj blocked a local road by slow walking, protesting against the proposed construction of a new railway in their neighborhood.

On 10 September 2021, contact center workers affiliated with the telecommunication branch of the UGL trade union gathered outside the National Institute for Social Security (INPS) offices in Milano (Milano, Lombardia) to call on the institution to apply a 'social clause' while integrating contact center workers. The event was part of a national day of protest.

On 2 April 2026, 15 truck drivers drove at 15 kmh over the Aflsuitdijk from Kornwerderzand (Friesland) to Den Oever (Noord-Holland) and back, to protest against the high fuel prices, significantly disrupting traffic. Protesters called on the government to lower fuel excise duties.

On 25 March 2023, about 15 people belonging to action group Active for Justice staged peaceful protests in front of several restaurants in Eindhoven (Noord-Brabant), demanding that they remove foie gras from their menus, citing the animal-unfriendly nature of the product.

On 21 April 2022, around 70 persons, including members of unions, locally elected politicians and members of MRAP, EELV, PCF and PS demonstrated in Privas. They denounced the fact that a candidate to the presidential election associated to the far-right ideology reached the stage of the second round of the elections.

On 21 July 2025, in the evening, under the motto 'Vigil against Weidel', around 900 people staged a protest in Regensburg (Bayern) against AfD leader Alice Weidel's planned attendance at the Castle Festival.

On 15 March 2022, striking haulers gathered with their vehicles at the entrance of the industrial area of Monastir (Sud Sardegna, Sardegna), blocking traffic, to protest against the increase in oil and gas prices.

On 2 July 2025, citizens and students blocked several sites in Novi Pazar, including the city administration and the magistral road towards Montenegro, voicing their dissatisfaction with the city's decision to keep pro-regime media as their sub-contractor, and denouncing the police interventions against peaceful citizens and students.

On 13 February 2021, activists affiliated to the KOD movement gathered for a rally in Gdansk, protesting against a newly proposed tax on online advertisement. They considered the proposal to be a form of pressure from the government against private, mostly oppositional, media.

On 30 September 2020, hundreds of people, predominantly the Armenian community in Spain, protested in front of the Turkish consulate in Barcelona - Gracia to protest against the 'Azerbaijan's full scale military attack' in Armenia.
On 18 February 2022, members and supporters of the SOR party protested in Briceni, against the increased gas prices, condemning the current PAS government.
On 22 September 2024, thousands of CD Tenerife football fans protested in Santa Cruz de Tenerife (Canarias) against the club's management model and the club's largest shareholder.
On 13 October 2022, mothers of children hospitalized in Warsaw gathered in front of a local health facility, complaining about delays of medical procedures of their children.

On 11 October 2025, more than 10,000 uniformed military personnel, including active-duty officers, non-commissioned officers, and retired military personnel from across Greece, rallied in Athens - Central Athens and marched to parliament against a Ministry of Defense bill and the creation of a new corps of non-commissioned officers (NCOs). They also demanded a salary increase and the restoration of bonus payments for both active service members and retirees. MAT riot police forces had lined up with police vehicles. Representatives of the protesters from 13 associations had a meeting with the senior manager of the Prime Minister's office.

On 25 January 2023, two demonstration marches arrived at San Vito alley in Campobello di Mazara (Trapani, Sicilia) outside one of the hideouts of a mafia boss to protest against the mafia. The marches started from Castelvetrano and Campobello di Mazara and were led by their Mayors (M5S and PD, respectively). Students, Mazara del Vallo bishop and a priest took part in the demonstration.

On 13 May 2023, between 300 and 400 people, including an LFI MP and members of the associations NADA (No to the expansion of Lille Lesquin Airport), ANV-COP21, Extinction Rebellion and Friends of the Earth gathered in front of the Lille-Lesquin airport in Lesquin to demonstrate against the proposed expansion of the airport.
On 21 July 2021, around 30 Petronor workers protested in Bilbao to complain about a collective dismissal affecting over 300 employees.

On 5 September 2022, at the call of CONFCOMMERCIO, residents and business owners gathered in Citta di Castello (Perugia, Umbria) to symbolically burn the latest energy bills in protest against the increase in energy prices, which will allegedly force many of them to close their businesses.

On 9 November 2025, residents demonstrated in Sassari (Sardegna) to protest the planned construction of a pigsty that would hold more than 1,000 pigs. Demonstrators demanded that competent authorities protect their health, water resources, and the value of their properties.

On 29 December 2022, a dozen Extinction Rebellion activists staged a protest in front and inside of the Cora supermarket in Brussels - Anderlecht, blocking the fish section to denounce the cooking of lobsters while they are still alive during Christmas and New Year's celebrations.

On 29 June 2022, members of the Athens Urban Transport Organization (OASA) workers' union participated in a 24-hour strike and a demonstration outside OASA headquarters in Athens demanding that a tender with privately operated KTEL intercity buses would not be extended.
On 26 April 2023, around 200 people, including members of ALG, demonstrated from the St. Thomas Church, through Kreuzberg, to Marx-Engels-Forum in Berlin - Mitte to call for climate protection.

On 22 June 2021, in the evening, women's organizations and neighborhood assemblies and collectives marched in Petralona in Athens - Central Athens holding banners against sexism, patriarchy and the culture of rape and domestic violence, following repeated incidents of abuse in their neighborhood. The protesters also shouted slogans for British-Greek Caroline Crouch killed by her husband and for other prominent cases of murdered women.
On 14 April 2021, activists occupied the Neckarinsel in Tubingen in solidarity with the activists protesting in the Dannenrod Forest and against the construction of a highway.

On 10 March 2026, in the afternoon, residents and members of the association The Main Road (La Via Maestra) staged a flashmob outside the Prefecture in Genova (Liguria) to protest all wars. Protesters also demanded peace worldwide.

On 21 February 2020, after the far-right motivated shooting in Hanau, about 180 people, including Jews and SPD politicians, commemorated in Hanau the victims of the attack and protested against the far-right violence.

On 9 March 2024, around 550 people gathered under the motto 'All Together Against Fascism' in Chemnitz (Sachsen) to protest against right-wing extremism, while around 400 people joined a Free Saxony counter-demonstration.
On 6 November 2021, around 1800 people protested in Barcelona against the rise in energy prices.
On 12 July 2023, several locals protested outside the water supply company headquarters in Galati, condemning the high tariffs.

On 19 November 2025, workers gathered at the Symbio hydrogen-fuel-cell plant in Saint-Fons (Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes) to denounce the progressive decline of their company and to urge Symbio's partner Stellantis to take responsibility and honor its financial commitments.

On 13 December 2021, Legambiente activists gathered outside the city hall in Torino to protest against the air pollution levels in big cities. The event was organized to mark the Clean Cities Campaign.
On 15 May 2023, hauliers obstructed traffic in Vallensbaek, Hovedstaden, to oppose the road tax on diesel large goods vehicles that was proposed by the government.
On 21 February 2019, in Topola, Serbia, citizens held an anti-government protest, part of a series of protests held throughout the country for several consecutive weeks.

On 9 May 2026, at the call of students, people from the Serbian diaspora and Serbian students gathered in Basel (Basel-Stadt) to support Serbian students demanding democracy, rule of law, and early elections. Protesters held 16 minutes of silence in memory of the 16 victims of Novi Sad train station canopy's collapse in 2024.
On 3 December 2022, about 20 Romanian oil refinery workers protested in Rijeka, demanding the urgent payment of their salaries.

On 13 May 2021, relatives of mafia victims, most of them females, gathered outside the Palace of Justice of Palermo (Palermo, Sicilia) to demand answers and justice from the Italian state for the death of their relatives.
On 23 February 2022, striking haulers gathered at the wheel of a few dozen vehicles for a protest near Racalmuto (Agrigento, Sicilia) to protest against the increase in oil and energy prices.
On 26 September 2024, at the call of CGT, Solvay employees blocked access to their factory in Salindres (Occitanie) to demand safe jobs amid news of downsizing.

On 15 January 2026, judicial staff in Tuzla Canton protested again in front of the Cantonal Government over the withholding of December salaries, despite a court order. The union warned of a total judicial collapse if their wage demands are not met and announced over 150 lawsuits.

On 27 May 2024, activists gathered for a rally in front of the national parliament in Bratislava, protesting against a new WHO-related agreement aimed at global disease control. They claimed the measures can be used for restriction of civic freedoms.
On 17 September 2022, people demonstrated in Schoenefeld at the Berlin Brandenburg Airport Willy Brandt (BER) airport for an extension of the ban on night flights and against aircraft noise.
On 13 November 2023, around 120 people held a torchlight procession in Fana, Bergen, to oppose the closure of a motorway in the area, claiming that it could affect local residents.

On 3 February 2023, around 100 people affiliated with FFF demonstrated in Freiburg im Breisgau (Baden-Wurttemberg) to protest against the nationwide expansion of the highway network and demand climate action.

On 11 January 2022, citizens called by the ANC protested in Tarragona demanding the truth about the 'terrorists' attacks on 17 August 2017. The demonstration was called following a new declaration before the Courts by a former police superintendent accused of an alleged corruption network with businesspeople and politicians. The defendant linked the attacks with an error committed by the National Intelligence Centre.

On 15 July 2025, a large group of Lazio Football Club supporters took to the streets in Roma - City Center (Lazio), marching from Corrado Ricci Square to the Fores, to protest the management of the Club and demand the resignation of its President, Claudio Lotito.

On 3 November 2023, trade union activists staged a blockade at a car workshop in Orebro to express their support and solidarity with the current strike against an American multinational car manufacturer.

On 28 September 2022, 4,000-8,000 people, mainly health workers, gathered for a protest at the Regional Agency of Health on Willy-Brandt avenue in Lille, against their exclusion from the Segur system.
On 14 November 2022, around 800 people, at the call of 'Halle Movement', demonstrated in Halle (Saale) for peace and no weapons. They marched from Hallmarkt to Riebeckplatz.

On 16 March 2024, under the motto 'Schopfheim remains colorful', and at the call of the diaconia, the protestant church, and the 'Working Group Integration' (Arbeitskreis Integration), around 600 people participated in a protest in Schopfheim (Baden-Wurttemberg) for democracy and against right-wing extremism. The protest was organized following reports about a secret meeting between AfD members and far-right activists in Potsdam in November 2023, during which remigration plans were discussed.

On 10 October 2021, activists gathered for a rally in Kazimierza Wielka. It was a part of a large string of events held in protest against the recent ruling of the Constitutional court of Poland, which allegedly jeopardizes the membership of the country in EU. The initiative was coordinated by the KOD movement.

On 9 November 2022, around 40 McDonald's employees, together with union delegates, association representatives and political activists, gathered in Toulouse. They demonstrated to denounce the 'racist, homophobic and sexist insults and comments made by their colleagues on a daily basis for months, as well as the lack of reaction of the management'.
On 11 October 2025, SNS supporters gathered in Novi Becej to march in support of Serbs in Kosovo, backing the government and opposing student-led protests and blockades.
On 1 October 2022, more than 300 people gathered for a protest in Montpellier, against the noise and pollution caused by traffic that has been rerouted to pass by their houses.

On 15 February 2022, people demonstrated in Sortland to oppose rising electricity prices in the country and to demand government take control over the electricity industry and electricity export to neighboring countries.
On 13 April 2023, 100 firefighters held a protest in Oviedo (Asturias) against the dismantling of their services and to denounce the lack of resources for the sector.
On 7 June 2020, several hundred motor bikers protested in Dresden against an impending driving ban.

On 28 September 2024, around 100 people, including far-right affiliates such as members of AF, gathered in Bordeaux (Nouvelle-Aquitaine). The event took place after the death of Philippine, a 19-year student who was found dead in the Bois de Boulogne on 21 September. The main suspect is a Moroccan man who had already been found guilty of rape in the past and was under the obligation to leave French territory (OQTF) at the time of Philippine's death. The protesters condemned 'mass migration', which they considered responsible for the increase in crime, and what they deemed the French justice's leniency towards foreign criminals.

On 8 December 2025, in the afternoon, about 50 residents of the Sa Calatrava neighborhood gathered in Palma de Mallorca (Islas Baleares) to protest the felling of 18 bellasombra trees scheduled by the city council.
On 16 January 2021, people protested in Sofia, demanding the resignation of the government cabinet and Prosecutor General Geshev.
On 8 July 2021, ambulance drivers protested in Chartres to call for a different status that doesn't define them as only drivers but also as health workers.

On 30 April 2022, around 100 members of the Kurdish community demonstrated in Lorient. They denounced the military operation conducted by Turkey in Southern Kurdistan, denouncing the alleged use of chemical weapons against civilians.
On 5 December 2022, over 100 people, at the call of the 'Freedom Messengers', demonstrated in Konigs Wusterhausen against inflation and the government's energy policy.

On 4 February 2022, activists gathered for a rally in Slovenj Gradec, criticizing the government and protesting against some of its controversial actions, including a planned purchase of expensive military equipment.

On 21 October 2019, the Mayor of East Samos organised a rally to protest for the 'decongestion' of the overcrowded migrant and refugee reception facility in Vathy, Samos. The vice regional governor of Samos, also representing the Aegean regional governor, and the Metropolitis of Samos also participated in the protest.

On 24 June 2025, activists from the Nature and Youth and Sami activists blocked the construction site at Repparfjorden, near Kvalsund, Troms og Finnmark, to protest against the establishment of the Nussir copper mine. Later, police personnel removed activists from the site after they failed to comply with police demands, several activists were detained.

On 16 June 2022, around 100 PCRM and PSRM supporters, led by PSRM city counsellors and PSRM and PCRM MPs, protested outside the parliament building in Chisinau - Buiucani, condemning the high inflation and the government's inaction.

On 6 September 2021, a group of people including a farmer, gathered in front of a 4G antenna in Mazeyrat-d'Allier. They denounced the installation of the antenna accused to cause sickness to his cows.

On 14 November 2020, around 90 far-right activists commemorated the NS 'Waffen SS' unit and the 'Bomb Holocaust' in Remagen. Around 400 activists from the far-left tried repeatedly to disrupt the far-right funeral march and blocked the way. Police kept both parties away from each other. Some far-left activists injured two police officers when they tried to break through the police barrier.
On 14 January 2021, health workers with a temporary job contract gathered outside the Molise Regional Council in Campobasso to demand a permanent job contract.

On 15 April 2026, around 60 prison guards, including FO and CFTC representatives, and National Deputy Clementine Autain (The Aftermath), blocked the entrance to the Villepinte prison in Villepinte (Ile-de-France) to protest against prison overcrowding. Protesters also denounced understaffing and stated that the prison needed 60 more guards.

On 6 September 2020, half a dozen Sardines Movement and More Europe activists gathered with banners in Pordenone to support the no-vote in the constitutional referendum to reduce the number of parliamentarians.

On 7 October 2023, about 55 women and men, including representatives of the SPD, the Left, the Greens, the church and associations of the city, protested in Grevesmuhlen (Nordwestmecklenburg, Mecklenburg-Vorpommern) for diversity and tolerance. The context of the demonstration is the ongoing protest against refugee accommodations in the region.

On 25 March 2025, around 30 people gathered outside the Court of Justice in Limoges (Nouvelle-Aquitaine). The event was part of a nationwide movement of judicial youth protection agents called by SNPES-PJJ/FSU to protest against the so-called 'Attal law', which aimed to prescribe harsher penalties against young offenders. The protesters considered the law too repressive.
On 15 May 2022, around 200 fans demonstrate in Valencia (Valencia) against the management of Quico Catalan and ask for his resignation.

On 20 April 2021, police officers demonstrated in front of the courthouse in Rouen, at the national call of the National Police Alliance and UNSA unions. They denounced the outcome of the trial of demonstrators who attacked and severely injured police officers in Viry Chatillon in 2016.
On 18 January 2023, KOD activists gathered for a rally in Krakow, protesting against alleged politicization of courts in Poland.

On 12 May 2026, around 40 people, including students and anarchist groups, demonstrated outside a restaurant in Torino (Piemonte) against the presence of MEP and National Future leader Roberto Vannacci, chanting anti-fascist slogans.

On 3 December 2025, at the call of JUPOL, police officers and union representatives protested outside the government delegation in Valencia (Valencia) to demand urgent reforms in response to rising violence against police, after a police officer was killed while on duty. Protesters denounced inadequate equipment, weak legal penalties for attacks, and a loss of authority, while calling for the Minister of Defense's resignation.

On 19 July 2024, people, including Bangladeshi community members, demonstrated in Jyvaskyla, Keski-Suomi, to oppose the ongoing violence and human rights abuses in Bangladesh and to draw attention to the excessive use of force by Bangladeshi authorities against student protesters.

On 20 September 2023, around 2,500 employees of the energy company Leag protested in Spremberg (Spree-Neisse, Brandenburg) to demand permanently higher remuneration. The protest occurred in the context of an 8-hour strike to increase pressure on the company in light of tariff negotiations with the IGBCE this Friday.

On 30 March 2022, Eugenio Montale High School students rallied outside their school in Rome - Gianicolense (Roma, Lazio) to protest against their school principal after she was accused of entertaining a relationship with one of the school's students.
On 28 December 2022, between 30 and 40 CGT delegates occupied the Pole Emploi Marine facility in Lorient, to demonstrate against the reform of unemployment insurance.

On 26 January 2025, a couple of hundred Turkish Cypriot residents of Dipkarpaz rallied blocking the road linking the village to the Apostolos Andreas monastery, a popular tourist destination, and demanded the road be completely rebuilt. The mayor (belonging to UBP), mukhtars, civil society organizations, council members and citizens participated in the action.

On 25 February 2026, around 50 members of the Etrepagny soccer club marched from the soccer stadium to the town hall in Etrepagny (Normandie) to protest against delays in the soccer field's renovation. The current state of the soccer field was deemed to endanger players during soccer games.

On 27 November 2020, between 3500 (according to the police) and 7000 people, including union members (CFDT, CGT, FO, FSU, SUD ), lawyers, and LDH activists, demonstrated in Nantes against a national security bill that they condemned as a violation of freedom of information, demonstrators' rights, and media rights, as well as the implementation of global surveillance of citizens. People allegedly threw projectiles at the police, who retaliated with tear gas. 17 people were arrested.

On 1 August 2022, SOR party members and supporters, including two SOR mayors and a district council president, protested outside the Appeal Court in Chisinau - Botanica, demanding the release of an arrested SOR MP.
On 13 June 2022, workers of call centers staged a protest in Leon (Castilla y Leon) called by the UGT and CCOO unions to demand a 'dignified' collective agreement.
On 29 July 2024, citizens and ecological activists protested in Arandelovac against Rio Tinto's lithium extraction project which has been revived by the government.

On 16 October 2024, around 2000 people (as per estimations of the Archive of Public Gathering), organized by the SEOS, along with representatives of oppositional political parties, protested in Loznica against lithium mining. The protest was initiated after the members of the Serbian Parliament did not adopt a law proposed by the opposition to ban lithium mining in the country.

On 17 February 2023, an unknown number of representatives of the police unions staged a protest in front of the residency of the Federal Minister of Independents in Bievre to denounce the lack of support of the federal government for their wage demands.

On 4 October 2024, female students from different local schools held a protest in Plasencia (Extremadura) to call on the local government to find a school transport solution that could accommodate all the students from the Navaconcejo and Cabezuela villages.

On 17 May 2026, about 250 people gathered on Peace Avenue at the statue of Jan Kaspar in Pardubice and marched along Peace Avenue through Pernstynske Square to the regional Czech Radio editorial office, organized by the Million Moments for Democracy association under the slogan 'Hands off the media'. The action ended at around 18:15 with the national anthem at the Automatic Mills. Participants demanded the withdrawal of a government bill transferring the financing of Czech Television and Czech Radio from license fees to the state budget.

Around 4 July 2022 (as reported), people gathered outside Parliament in Valletta (South Eastern) at the call of Beltin Residents (Residenti Beltin) to protest against a legal notice allowing them to play music until 1am in several streets in Valletta, including some residential areas.

On 3 February 2022, Sheraton Hotel workers gathered, with the support of FILCAMS CGIL, FISASCAT CISL and UILTUCS (UIL) union branch delegates, outside Villa Borghese in Rome - Pinciano (Roma, Lazio) to protest against the recent announcement of the dismissal of 164 of them.
On 4 October 2020, people protested in Sofia demanding the resignation of Prime Minister Borisov and chief prosecutor Geshev over alleged corruption and links to mafia.
On 1 March 2022, people working at the customs agency gathered in Torino to protest against the lack of personnel. CONFSAL took part in the demonstration.

On 18 August 2023, protesters and members of Paris Animals Zoopolis rallied outside the Jardin des Plantes in Paris to call for 5 orangutans to be moved from the Menagerie to an animal sanctuary due to poor conditions. The rally was part of the World Orangutan Day.

On 28 December 2021, about 40 police officers of the asylum seekers' center in Ter Apel protested in Ter Apel (Groningen) to denounce their high workload. The event was organized by four police unions: ANPV, ACP, NPB and Equipe.

On 8 February 2025, at the call of the Oasis Caravanning Association (l'Associacio de Caravaning Oasis) and the Autonomous Motorhome Platform (Plataforma Autocaravanes Autonoma), around 200 vehicles took part in a protest convoy in Palma de Mallorca (Islas Baleares) against a new law banning the use of caravans as housing. The legislation, approved by the local government, imposed fines for sleeping in a motorhome. Protesters argued that the law unfairly targeted individuals who relied on caravans due to high rental prices, holding banners stating 'Parking is not camping. Regulate, don't ban.'

On 30 May 2020, several thousand people marched through Sarajevo, Bosnia and Herzegovina, demanding the government step down after a series of corruption scandals. Leaders of several oppositional parties attended.

On 22 April 2023, more than 300 people, including Angry Bikers members, gathered a parking lot in the Caer area in Normanville then reassembled with 100 more people in the city center in Evreux for a procession at the prefecture. The event was called for by the Federation of Angry Bikers to denounce the Council of State's decision to force the government to relaunch technical control requirement for motorized two and three-wheel vehicles.
On 16 May 2024, people, including parents and students, held a protest at the Los Alamos school in Murcia (Murcia) to demand the lack of air conditioning systems in the summer season.

On 24 July 2025, at the call of the Workers' Unitary Central (Central Unitaria de Traballadores - CUT), workers of Vertisol protested outside the factory in Morana (Galicia) to demand additional workplace safety measures, following an incident in which a worker lost three fingers.
On 24 May 2018: Citizens protested in the main square in Tirana against a hydropower construction, which would disrupt the 30 kilometer natural length of the Valbona river.

On 23 June 2022, Pro Life and Family activists demonstrated against the support given by regional authorities to the organization of a pride parade, in Perugia (Perugia, Umbria). The demonstration was also attended by members of Lega and two regional councilors.

On 28 June 2025, citizens gathered in Blagoevgrad to protest the country's entry into the Eurozone next year, demanding the preservation of the Bulgarian lev and the rejection of the euro. The protesters claimed the euro is being imposed on the Bulgarian people by the corrupt ruling elites in the GERB party and others, that average Bulgarians are against it, and that a referendum should be organized to determine the outcome of this issue.

On 25 January 2020, about 1,600 far left activists demonstrated in Leipzig-Connewitz against the ban of the left website Indymedia. Rioters damaged public infrastructure during the demonstration, launched pyrotechnic and threw stones at police officers, injuring 13 policemen. Journalists were also attacked. 6 rioters were arrested.

On 12 October 2020, over 100 police officers and administrative employees demonstrated in front of the police station in Pau, at the call of the SGP union. They denounced the riot against the police station of Champigny-sur-Marne days before and denounced the violence and threats that they experience.

On 28 May 2021, more than 500 residents of the Samoranovo village protested in front of the Municipal building in Dupnitsa, Bulgaria, complaining about the lack of water in the settlement and calling for the resignation of the mayor.
On 19 June 2021, people staged a vigil in Lindau (Bodensee) to protest against anti-Semitism.

On 19 February 2021, around 500 people protested in Basel to pay tribute to the victims of a mass shooting in Hanau that happened on 19 February 2020 and take a stand against right-wing terror. They gathered not to forget nor forgive far-right extremism.
On 26 September 2020, at least 25 members of the Somme Memorial Flute Band paraded through Bangor. The parade was marked 'sensitive' by the Parades Commission but no conditions were imposed.
On 10 January 2020, FFF activists and students protested in Stuttgart against Siemen's plan to invest in a coal mine project in Australia.
On 24 February 2022, striking haulers occupied the Sant'Onofrio motorway exit in Sant'Onofrio (Vibo Valentia, Calabria) to protest against the increase in oil and gas prices.
Around 19 January 2020 (from 19 - 20 January), Russoli high school in Cascina was occupied by the students to protest against the poor conditions of school buildings.
On 28 April 2022, citizens of Puigcerda and members of the CDR gathered in Puigcerda (Girona) to protest against the organization of the 2030 Olympic Games.
On Dec. 2, 2018: Citizens from Troyan blocked the road towards Oreshak protesting against the high fuel prices and low living standard.
On 10 May 2021, activists gathered for a demonstration in Krakow near a local zoo, protesting against keeping animal in captivity.

On 3 October 2021, anti-fascists took part in a rally on Cable Street in Wapping to mark the anniversary of the Battle of Cable Street when anti-fascists clashed with police over a scheduled march organized by British Union of fascists led by Oswald Mosely. Labour MP Jeremy Corbyn as well as representatives of the RMT Union and Unison were present.
On 18 July 2022, KOD activists gathered for a rally in Zielona Gora, protesting against alleged politicization of courts in Poland.
On 11 June 2021, students and family members of Santa Maria de Gracia protested in Murcia, demanding a new electrical system in the building. The UGT trade union was involved in the protest.

On 2 January 2022, about 500 people demonstrated in the Vohwinkle section of Wuppertal to denounce a decision by the Higher Administrative Court in Munster according to which around 1,500 trees in the Osterholz forest of Vohwinkle-Wuppertal could be felled.
On 27 October 2021, activists affiliated with the Women's Strike movement gathered for a rally in Czestochowa, demanding higher solidarity with refugees stranded at the border with Belarus.

On 10 January 2025, around 200 penitentiary policemen and officers from the County Police Inspectorate Bacau protested in front of the Bacau Penitentiary and the County Police Inspectorate Bacau in Bacau, against salary reductions caused by the 'little train' ordinance, which resulted in monthly losses of 1,400-2,000 lei. Some of the prison officers refused to go on shift for an hour and a half.
On 19 December 2021, activists gathered for a rally in Olsztyn, protesting against a new law on media ownership, which they perceive as a harmful pressure of the government against independent media.

On 31 July 2024, at the call of CGIL, FP CGIL, SILP CGIL and SILF CGIL, workers in the security sector demonstrated in Bari (Puglia) against the lack of staff and the salaries, which are considered inadequate. A delegation of protesters met with the mayor (PD) and the prefect. This event is part of a national demonstration in support of the renewal of the contract for military and law enforcement officers, including police, prison police, Carabinieri and Guardia di Finanza.

On 29 March 2025, more than 1,000 people, including residents of Talence and Pessac, demonstrated outside the Bordeaux Airport in Merignac (Gironde) (Nouvelle-Aquitaine) to demand the closure of the second runway at the airport, citing heavy noise pollution.
On 25 August 2023, employees of the finance departments protested in Iasi over announced wage cuts.
On 19 November 2021, Extinction Rebellion's Forest group protested outside the office of Metsahallitus (a state-owned forest enterprise) in Oulu, demanding for improved forestry policy and practices.

On 21 December 2019, Albanians gathered outside the Prime Minister's Office in Tirana to protest the third meeting of 'Mini Schengen' initiative between Balkan leaders, and in particular Serbia's president Alexandar Vucic's presence in Tirana. They denounced Vucic's denial of massacres committed by the Serbian regime of Slobodan Milosevic, and the fact that Vucic was minister of Information when massacres took place.

On 10 January 2026, at 2pm, around 60 people protested outside the Prefecture in Angers (Pays de la Loire) to show solidarity with the Venezuelan people and condemn US foreign aggression. The event was part of a wider mobilization opposing US military intervention in Venezuela, which resulted in the abduction of President Nicolas Maduro and his wife on 3 January 2026, and aimed to demonstrate solidarity with the civilian population.
On 23 May 2020, around 50 people protested in Neubrandenburg under the motto 'No space for right-wing ideology and conspiracy theories'. The protest was organised by the SPD.

On 16 September 2020, members of Police Salary Justice (JUSAPOL) gathered in front of the Congress of Deputies in Madrid - Centro (Madrid) to protest over the lack of a Suicide Prevention Protocol within the State's security forces. Protesters also complained about the 'deepest condolences' expressed by the President of the Government because of the death of a former member of Basque Homeland and Liberty (ETA) in prison after he committed suicide.
On 18 February 2022, members and supporters of the SOR party protested in Soroca, against the increased gas prices, condemning the current PAS government.

On 2 June 2022, transport workers protested in Sofia in front of the Ministry of Transport, a continuing of massive national protests held in May. They demand that their salaries go up in line with increased gas prices and that plans to expand the toll system be suspended.
On 19 November 2021, a Fridays for Future climate strike gathered by the Parliament in Helsinki, demanding climate action.

On 17 September 2023, an unknown number of activists and sympathizers of Extinction Rebellion staged a protest action in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland), blocking traffic on the Utrechtsebaan A12 highway, to call on the government to stop funding fossil fuel companies and projects. Police forces responded with a water cannon and arrested up to 400 people.

On 4 October 2022, on the occasion of the visit of managers of the company to the premises in Bagnoli della Rosandra (Trieste, Friuli-Venezia Giulia), Wartsila workers staged a demonstration to protest against the decision of the company to close that branch. CGIL, CISL and UIL took part in the demonstration.

On 6 February 2020, about 400 people, including students, women and Grannies against the Right, protested in Erfurt following the election of a FDP candidate as the Minister-President of Thuringia. Protesters accused the Landtag of election fraud.
On 26 June 2021, around 40 members of the yellow vests movement demonstrated at the Sdis roundabout in Saint-Avit. They called for social and fiscal justice.

On 22 December 2020, members of the Workers Commissions trade union gathered in Sevilla, demanding to hire public sector staffing for the new Military Hospital. Protesters fear that the services would be outsourced.

On 12 June 2024, around 100 people gathered in Tours (Centre-Val de Loire) to demonstrate against far-right ideology and in support of the new Popular Front, the union between left-wing parties for the forthcoming legislative elections. The gathering took place after the National Rally (RN) came first in the European elections in France and President Emmanuel Macron announced the dissolution of the National Assembly on 9 June, raising fears of a government led by the far-right party.

On 16 November 2025, CGT union members and port workers demonstrated in Vigo (Galicia) to demand compliance with the metalworkers' collective bargaining agreement. Up to six police vehicles and several officers charged against three union members, injuring one of them, who then required medical attention. One demonstrator kicked an officer in the chest, requiring him to be taken to the hospital.

On 2 February 2020, about 70 people, including suspected Iraqi refugees, protested in Vienna - Inner City (Wien), at Stock-im-Eisen-Platz, for peace in Iraq and in solidarity with the Iraqi liberation movement.
On 6 June 2021, local residents of the Mar de Tambo housing state protested in Poio against eight houses' demolition order.

On 25 September 2020, a dozen activists of Vlaams Belang staged a protest action at the Antwerpse Ring highway in Berchem against the imminent formation of a federal government without Flemish majority in the Federal Parliament, by hanging a banner from a bridge asking bypassers to sound the horn.

On 23 September 2025, around 100 people, including CGT leader Sophie Binet, gathered in front of the Valeo site in Limoges (Nouvelle-Aquitaine) to protest against a planned social plan cutting 83 jobs. Workers staged a walkout and displayed banners denouncing the layoffs, arguing that they would eliminate more than a third of the site's workforce. Binet criticized Valeo for relocating production to Turkey with publicly subsidized machinery.

On 29 May 2026, striking employees working at the German Rochling factory picketed outside the factory in Decines-Charpieu (Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes) to protest against the factory's closure on 30 June 2026, causing the redundancy of 41 employees. Protesters started their strike on 11 May 2026 for the same motive.

On 23 September 2025, residents of the Aerodrom neighborhood of Skopje protested over the persistent stench and pollution from the Vardarishte landfill. The protesters urged Skopje's municipal leaders to unite behind a solution, accelerate cleanup and stop further dumping after a fire worsened air quality. Protesters have been taking place on consecutive days for weeks.

On 11 October 2024, 100 students, at the nationwide call of SE, held a protest in Albacete (Castilla La Mancha) to denounce the lack of transparency of the newly implemented college entrance exam and demand more information about the examination model. Students blocked one side of the road. The protest was followed by a strike.
On 17 February 2020, more than 1,000 workers protested in Villablino to demand a fair transition after the closure of the coal mines.

On 28 June 2023, overnight, rioters clashed with police forces and vandalized and set fire to street furniture in Hem. The event was part of a national wave of riots and demonstrations denouncing police violence and demanding justice in the wake of the shooting and subsequent death of 17-year-old Nahel M. by a police officer in Nanterre on 27 June 2023.

On 8 July 2025, hundreds of protesters marched on the Royal Courts of Justice in London - Westminster (England) to oppose the All England Club's GBP200 million expansion plan for the Wimbledon tennis grounds. The demonstration coincided with the opening of a two-day High Court hearing where residents and campaigners challenged the legality of planning permission granted for the development.
On 1 May 2022, people gathered in Assisi (Perugia, Umbria) at the call of CGIL, CISL, and UIL on the occasion of Labor Day to call for peace and social justice.

On 13 September 2025, SNS supporters, along with local officials and directors of state-owned enterprises, gathered in Cacak to express support for the government and oppose student-led protests and blockades. Citizens and students gathered to counter-protest. Tensions escalated with two groups throwing water and eggs at each other.

On 14 March 2022, students blocked the access to the high school of Sartene. They denounced French State's responsibility in the attempted murder against a Corsican militant by a Jihadi prisoner at the prison of Arles and called for the liberation of all Corsican nationalist militants.

On 25 February 2023, at the call of the 'Loveable and Life worthy Ruthen' group, around 100 people demonstrated in front of the building on Thiestrasse in Rethen in Laatzen to call for the preservation of the Dismer barn.

On 9 December 2023, at the call of the local mayor (political affiliation not specified), around 150 people gathered in Commentry (Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes) against hatred and to advocate fraternity, following the discovery of anti-Semitic, racist and homophobic tags in a local secondary school.
On 21 January 2022, around 70 vehicles marched from Espiel (Cordoba) until Azuaga (Badajoz), demanding the construction of a highway connecting Badajoz with Cordoba and Granada.
On 17 March 2018, 2018 in Osijek, Croatia, citizens protested over cats being poisoned by unknown perpetrators in the city.

On 17 August 2024, an unknown number of police officers protested before a union meeting in Enschede (Overijssel) to demand that their jobs be considered as 'heavy' so that they could benefit from the country's Early Retirement Scheme (RVU).
On 17 July 2023, hairdressers and beauty workers held a protest in Bilbao (Bizkaia, Pais Vasco) to demand the restitution of reduced VAT to hairdressers, beauty salons and barbershops.
On 27 June 2022, truck drivers carried out a road blockade in Miramas at the call of the CGT and CFDT unions. They denounced their salary that does not reflect repeated inflations.
On 25 June 2020, several workers form the non-profit sector staged a protest at l'Enjambee in Namur to demand more support from regional authorities.

On 11 October 2020, tens of Turkish Cypriots rallied in Northern Cyprus at the Deryneia crossing point holding Turkish flags as a response to the Greek Cypriot riots on the other side of the crossing point. There was strong police and military presence.
On 11 January 2021, locals protested in Goianul Nou against the construction of a car service center in the middle of the village.

On 12 October 2022, around 100 students' parents gathered in front of the police station in Nanterre, calling for the release of 14 students arrested after recent clashes with the police in front of the Joliot-Curie High School.
On 30 January 2019, approximately 30 people protested outside the PSD regional office in Sibiu, condemning the government's attacks against the judiciary and the anti-corruption institutions.
On 8 October 2022, several thousand activists, including representatives of labor unions, gathered for a rally in Bratislava, protesting against high prices and inflation.

On 12 June 2025, around 50 people, including SNES-FSU affiliates, gathered in Dax (Nouvelle-Aquitaine) to pay tribute to a 31-year-old school supervisor who was fatally stabbed by a student in Nogent on 10 June 2025, denouncing school insecurity.

On 4 July 2024, about 50 protesters and members of the CGT and FSU-SNU rallied at Jeanne-Hachette Square in Beauvais (Hauts-de-France) to demonstrate. The event was part of a nationwide wave of demonstrations against far-right ideology and in support of an open society, and took place after the National Rally (RN) came first in the European elections in France and President Emmanuel Macron announced the dissolution of the National Assembly on 9 June 2024, prompting snap legislative elections and raising fears of a government led by the far-right party.

On 18 April 2022, former Montenegro Airlines workers protested in front of the Ministry of Capital Investments in Podgorica. The workers demanded that the government link their service length and payment of their remaining salaries.

On 28 October 2025, at the nationwide call of SE, around 300 students protested in Caceres (Extremadura) to demand that the central government implement measures to combat bullying in schools, after a minor who was harassed by schoolmates died by suicide in Sevilla. Protesters called for stronger accountability and protection measures in schools.

On 11 April 2026, police and military forces intervened to remove a blockade on O'Connell Street in Dublin (Dublin), which had been ongoing since 7 April by protesters affiliated with The People of Ireland Against Fuel Prices movement, an ongoing series of nationwide demonstrations across Ireland, which began on 6 April 2026 in response to sharply rising fuel prices and broader cost-of-living pressures. Vehicles were escorted away from the street.

On 6 May 2022, in the morning, FSP police union delegates, as well as Fervicredo - 'Wounded and Victims of Crime and Duty' ('Feriti e Vittime della criminalita e del Dovere'), gathered outside the Tribunal of Trieste (Trieste, Friuli-Venezia Giulia) to express solidarity with the relatives of the victims and demand justice for the death of two police officers at the hands of a Dominican man on 4 October 2019 at the police headquarters of Trieste.
On 23 August 2025, SNS supporters gathered in Loznica to express support for the government and oppose student-led protests and blockades.

On 31 May 2024, at the call of FFF, around 70 people, including 'Grannies for Future' (Omas for Future), students, and members of the 'Alliance for democracy and tolerance' (Bundnis fur Demokratie und Toleranz), participated in a protest in Biberach (Baden-Wurttemberg) for climate protection and democracy, and to draw attention to the importance of the EU in tackling the climate crisis. The protest was organized as part of FFF's international climate strike to call for an EU-wide phase-out of coal, oil and gas by 2035, and a doubling of investments in renewable energies and climate-neutral industries.

On 26 February 2022, hundreds of people, among them students and journalists, gathered in Pia Square in Anzio (Roma, Lazio) to protest against organized crime ('Ndrangheta) following the Tritone investigation.

On 24 November 2025, around 60 Gerstube employees and the Mayor Barbara Neto (UDR) gathered in front of the town hall in Vic-Fezensac (Occitanie) to protest against inadequate severance terms, the lack of real support after the factory's destruction by fire, and what they see as the company's unwillingness to provide dignified conditions for their impending layoffs.

On 12 August 2025, activists again gathered in front of a local pig farm near Karstna, protesting against the planned mass slaughter of pigs due to an infection, claiming the healthy animals should be preserved. An ERK politician also joined them.

On 11 November 2024, over 5,000 high school students from San Giorgio a Cremano and Portici, as well as members of unspecified local governments, marched from Massimo Troisi Square to Villa Vannucchi in Napoli (Campania) to commemorate Santo Romano, a 19-year-old killed in San Sebastiano al Vesuvio, and to protest against youth violence. The peaceful demonstration featured testimonies and appeals promoting mutual respect, peace, and solidarity.

On 26 May 2023, residents of Ruse protested after a young woman died a couple of hours after delivering a healthy baby earlier this month. The protesters demand accountability for her death from the hospital, which denies any wrongdoing.

On 17 September 2024, Motvind Norway activists demonstrated in Drammen, Viken, to oppose wind power development in the country. The demonstration was a part of the nationwide peaceful action staged in various locations of Norway.

On 31 January 2026, at around 3 pm, at the call of Women Defend Rojava Gottingen and the RiseUp4Rojava alliance, under the motto 'Defend the women's revolution: the path to peace!', around 700 people, including members of the Kurdish community, staged a protest in Gottingen (Niedersachsen) against attacks by Syrian government forces on the Kurdish self-administration in North and East Syria, opposing EU and German support for the Syrian transitional government. The event was part of a wider demonstration movement against the clashes between Kurdish militias and the Syrian armed forces in the Kurdish-controlled areas of Syria.

On 5 May 2023, pilots and airline workers held a protest before the Ministry of Transport in Madrid - San Blas-Canillejas (Madrid) against the application of the minimum services when there is a strike. The protest was summoned by the Spanish Union of Air Line Pilots (Sepla), USO, the Union of Airline Passenger Cabin Crew (Sitcpla), and the Spanish Union Association of Aeronautical Maintenance Technicians (Asetma).

Around 25 January 2024 (as reported), people staged a protest in Stralsund (Mecklenburg-Vorpommern), advocating against the AfD. The protest was prompted by concerns over a secret meeting between AfD representatives and extremists, discussing mass deportations of individuals with German citizenship and migrant background, leading to a heightened awareness and mobilization against right-wing ideologies in various cities.
On 22 June 2023, over 500 local police agents held a protest in Vitoria-Gasteiz (Araba, Pais Vasco) to demand salary and labor improvements.
On 24 June 2021, climate activists occupied the natural area Tornsangerland in Amager district of Copenhagen to block the planned construction work on the housing complex.

On 25 February 2022, striking haulers gathered for a protest at various motorway exits in Cerignola (Foggia, Puglia) to denounce the increase in oil and gas prices. The permanent gathering was terminated on the same day.

On 3 December 2020, over 100 childcare professionals gathered in front of the Departmental council of Herault in Montpellier. They demanded a re-evaluation of their status for their inclusion in the Segur agreements, on health and salary increase.
On 28 May 2020, at least 45 parents of students at a private college in Ortakoy, in northern Nicosia protested outside the school against the increase in school fees.

On 12 February 2022, anti-austerity campaigners gathered in Edinburgh to call for the government to intervene as household energy bills rise and freeze prices. This event was organised by the People's Assembly.

On 3 July 2023, people gathered outside the town hall in Vierville-sur-Mer in support of local public officials following multiple attacks on local administrators and administrations, notably in L'Hay-les-Roses, during the wave of riots and demonstrations following the shooting of Nahel M. by a police officer on 27 June 2023. The event was part of a nationwide rally day called by AMF outside French town halls and other public and municipal buildings. Mayor Antoine de Bellaigue took part in the event.
