On 14 February 2025, at the call of Grannies For Future (Omas for Future), around 300 people protested in Ingolstadt (Bayern) for climate protection. The event was part of a wider protest movement focused on climate protection ahead of the elections.

On 16 November 2021, several dozen Ferropem workers gathered in front of the Chateau-Feuillet site in La Lechere at the call of CGT to protest against the maintenance of the job protection plan (PSE). During the demonstration they set a few pallets on fire.

On 29 October 2022, people, at the call of the Querdenken movement, demonstrated in Dresden for peace, freedom, human rights, democracy, separation of powers, and politician liability. People gathered for a counter-demonstration and against far-right movements.

On 8 March 2021, around 200 people, including anti-fascist activists, protested in Duisburg on the occasion of International Women's Day under the motto: 'The crisis is in the system - Together against patriarchy and capitalism'.
On 2 October 2020, people protested in Sofia demanding the resignation of Prime Minister Borisov and chief prosecutor Geshev over alleged corruption and links to mafia.

On 1 September 2021, around 50 people protested in Schweinfurt on the occasion of 'Anti-War Day'. The exact reason for the protest was not reported. It was organized by the DGB, Initiative gegen das Vergessen, the Schweinfurt Alliance against Nuclear Power, the German Peace Community, the unemployment initiative Sali, the DGB youth and International Catholic Peace Movement.

On 12 July 2022, protesters gathered in front of the parliament in Tirana to voice their opposition to an initiative by the government to give up the Butrint National Park, a Roman-era amphitheater, to a private concessionaire for 10 years.
On 3 November 2021, 150 workers of an arms factory from central Bosnia protested in Sarajevo, Bosnia and Herzegovina, demanding their salaries because they have not been paid in 5 months.
On 7 January 2026, at the call of LFI, people gathered in front of the town hall of Argenteuil (Ile-de-France) to demand the re-opening of the local emergency homeless shelter.

On 23 September 2024, about 200 people, including residents and representatives of local committees, took to the streets in Chiaiano (Campania) to protest against the closure of the local police station. On 27 December 2022, residents of Stip protested the sand mining from the Bregalnica river, which they claim will disturb the riverbeds close to the land they cultivate.

On 3 February 2025, in the morning, between 30 and 40 people, including members of the anti-A69 highway movement, protested outside the courthouse in Toulouse (Occitanie) to demand the release of Louna, a 25-year-old trans activist detained in a men's prison in Tarbes. On 14 March 2026, in the morning, protesters gathered food items inside a supermarket in Manchester (England) and left the store without paying for them, as part of a protest against poverty, wealth inequality and the cost of living. On 26 January 2025, following leaked cell phone calls of the last moments of the victims of the Tempe rail disaster, protesters rallied in Geraki at the call of the association of the victims' families. The protesters demanded justice and accused the government of a cover-up. This was part of a large mobilization in more than 150 nationwide and international locations with the slogan 'I Have No Oxygen', the last words of one of the victims.

On 14 April 2026, around 40 people, including municipal representatives (PSOE) and business representatives, blocked the A-129 road near Sarinena (Aragon) to oppose the poor state of local roads, calling for urgent improvements to ensure road safety.
On 24 February 2022, striking haulers gathered for a protest at the port of Marghera (Venezia, Veneto) to protest against the increase in oil and gas prices.
On 5 July 2020, citizens gathered in Navas de Estena (Ciudad Real) to express support to the Mayor of the village who suffered a violent attack.

On 28 January 2022, in the afternoon, over 5,000 students, including OSA activists and Lupa movement affiliates, gathered near Santa Maria Maggiore Basilica before marching towards Dell'Esquilino square in Rome - City Center (Roma, Lazio) to demand more safety and less labor precarity for students and denounce the country's work-study program following the death, of a work accident, of an 18-year-old student from Udine while doing an internship in Lauzacco on 21 January 2022. On 3 February 2025, around two dozen activists gathered in Leipzig (Sachsen) in front of a stairway leading to a CDU office to protest. Earlier, also a separate assembly with about 15 people had been registered outside the Madlerpassage. The protest was organized by the socialist student collective and opposed the 'alliance between CDU and AfD,' condemning the criminalization of refugees and advocating for the preservation of the Self-Determination Act.
On 12 April 2021, citizens protested in Cartagena (Murcia) against the railway route project of the high-speed train to Cartagena.

On 17 January 2026, around 2000 people, mostly Iranian community members, gathered in Gothenburg (Goteborg), Vastra Gotaland, to oppose the ruling regime in Iran, to show their solidarity with the ongoing protests in Iran and to oppose the Iranian government's crackdown on demonstrations.

On 8 April 2026, ACOD-CGSP, ACV-CSC and VSOA-SLFP union members gathered at Hasselt station and drove through the center in Hasselt (Vlaanderen) to protest the planned budget cuts at public transport company De Lijn. Protesters feared service would deteriorate significantly as a result of these cuts.
On 27 June 2024, post office workers protested in Sarinena (Aragon) to denounce the lack of personnel.

On 24 June 2021, citizens protested in San Juan de Aznalfarache (Sevilla) to express support for multiculturalism. They condemned the stigmatization of the migrant population during Vox's political party last public act in the town.

On 13 April 2026, striking lawyers, the Mayor Regis Juanico (Generation.s) and associations, including SOS Domestic Violence (SOS Violences Conjugales - SOS-VC), gathered outside the Law Court in Saint-Etienne (Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes). The event was part of a nationwide strike movement by lawyers opposing the proposed 'SURE' law, arguing that it would expand the reach of criminal courts and infringe upon defendants' rights to a fair trial.
On 17 August 2022, residents of Cigacice gathered for a rally, demanding an investigation of a large-scale pollution of the Odra River.

On 26 March 2023, people, mostly affiliated with 'Polo Alternativo' and M5S representatives, took to the streets in Terni (Terni, Umbria) to protest against the decision to construct a sewage sludge drying plant for the entire region.

On 3 April 2021, at night, around 40 young persons threw mortar fireworks and Molotov cocktails at around 20 police officers in Evreux. They also set trash bins on fire following a message on social media calling for the demonstration, although the reason for the riot was not specified. No fatalities nor injuries were reported.

On 5 December 2025, in the morning, at the call of the initiative School Strike Against Conscription (Schulstreik gegen Wehrpflicht), students and supporters staged a protest in Leipzig (Sachsen) against the planned new military service law, criticizing the government for reintroducing conscription, including mandatory questionnaires and screenings for 18-year-old men and demanding peace-oriented policies. On 28 June 2022, Geomethane gas and electricity workers gathered in front of their factory in Manosque to call for an increase in their salaries.

On 28 November 2023, at the call of CGT, around 100 striking Sanofi employees and national deputy Francois Ruffin (LFI) gathered for a picket line outside the company's headquarters in Gentilly (Ile-de-France) to protest against the relocation of part of Sanofi's industrial production abroad.

On 26 September 2021, several dozen people staged a protest in Tessenderloo to denounce the imminent contstruction of a gas central in their neighborhood.

On 4 April 2022, postmen demonstrated at the headquarters of the post office in Saint-Genis-des-Fontaines at the call of the SUD and CGT unions. They called for a bonus to deliver campaign mails in view of the presidential election.

On 5 June 2018, 2018: Growers of cherries from Stara Zagora protested against low purchase prices. They gathered at the Stara Zagora road junction on the Trakia highway and poured a few boxes of fruit on the ground.

On 26 March 2021, fishers protested in their boats in A Coruna port against the proposed EU regulation on common fisheries policy, introducing regulation on electronic fishing logbooks and satellite-recorded vessel geo-location. Protesters complained about the 'criminalization' of their labor sector.

On 29 January 2025, taxi drivers, including the mayor of Jaen (PP), called by Taxi National Association (Antaxi-Asociacion Nacional del Taxi) and locally by Andalusian Taxi Freelancers (FAAT-Andaluza de Autanomos del Taxi), Tele-Taxi Jerez, Association of Taxi Drivers of Rota (asociacion de taxistas de Rota), held a protest in Jerez de la Frontera (Andalucia) against skyrocketing insurance costs and demanded government intervention to cap policy hikes and ensure the sector's survival amid rising expenses.

On 11 July 2023, activists from the Vegan Activism Denmark demonstrated outside of a luxury chain store in Copenhagen, calling on brand representatives to stop using animal products, including natural fur and leather.

On 10 November 2022, students staged a protest under the windows of the rector's office in Pavia (Lombardia) to ask to be able to eat their meals in the classrooms where lessons are held and to create dedicated spaces.

On 15 March 2022, striking haulers gathered with their vehicles at the entrance of the industrial area of Samatzai (Cagliari, Sardegna), blocking traffic, to protest against the increase in oil and gas prices.
On 10 June 2020, around 100 refugees protested in Frankfurt-Bonames against the living conditions in refugee accommodations.

On 10 December 2025, residents dissatisfied with the country's governance held a protest in Svishtov. Participants demanded the government's resignation, denouncing corruption, and displaying placards calling for accountability and the removal of Boyko Borissov and Delyan Peevski from power.

On 10 January 2023, around 50 prefecture and police headquarter workers staged a demonstration in Florence (Firenze, Toscana) to protest against their dismissal. On 16 October 2021, around 20 members of the L214 Ethics & Animals organization gathered in front of a Burger King restaurant in Feytiat. They denounced the chicken rearing practices of the company.
On 28 August 2023, more than 200 people protested in Essen (Nordrhein-Westfalen) for the preservation of the 'deinKult Cafe Essen' in Essen-Altenessen (Essen, Nordrhein-Westfalen).

On 12 October 2020, around 30 police officers and administrative employees demonstrated in front of the police station in Sarreguemines, at the call of the SGP union. They denounced the riot against the police station of Champigny-sur-Marne days before and denounced the violence and threats that they experience.
On 29 September 2020, employees of Mecafi blocked the access to the factory in Chatellerault. They denounced the plan of the company to cut 242 jobs out of 500.

On 30 June 2025, citizens blocked the railway road connecting Belgrade and the Montenegro seaside in Lazarevac, protesting against the police's excessive use of force against students, and numerous reported injuries and arrests.
On 11 October 2020, parents of children going to kindergarten gathered outside Cremona city hall to protest against a public exhibition. They claim that the art works are ambiguous and deceptive.

On 5 January 2026, in the evening, at the call of political parties such as JC, around 100 people gathered in Besancon (Bourgogne-Franche-Comte) to demonstrate. The event was part of a wider national mobilization opposing US military intervention in Venezuela, which resulted in the abduction of President Nicolas Maduro and his wife on 3 January 2026, and aimed to demonstrate solidarity with the civilian population.
On 7 March 2020, around 30 student protesters took part in a FridaysForFuture climate strike in Maynooth, Co. Meath.

On 14 February 2025, in the afternoon, at the call of the local women's shelter, around 50 people, mostly women, participated in a dance protest at the Rhein-Gallery in Ludwigshafen (Baden-Wurttemberg) as part of the global 'One Billion Rising' campaign against violence towards women and girls.

On 7 April 2024, students of the art school of Thessaloniki held a performance protest in Aristotelous square with the title 'Save art' to highlight their school's problems and to protest against legislative changes that put art students on a par with school leavers for state pay and qualifications. The students performed and voiced concerns about their school infrastructure.

On 8 March 2023, protesters carrying placards and banners rallied outside the Greek embassy in Nicosia over the Tempe rail disaster, the worst in Greece's history, and the longstanding deficiencies of Greece's railways, demanding a full inquiry and an end to privatizations. 2 Cypriot students were among the 57 who died in the collision.
On 18 June 2021, between 1,200 to 3,000 Fridays for Future supporters protested in Hamburg - Hamburg-Mitte (Hamburg), in Jungfernstieg, for more climate action.

On 5 December 2022, dozens of students occupied the Michelangelo, Dante-Alberti and Rodolico high schools in Florence (Firenze, Toscana) to oppose the newly-elected Italian government and its school-related policies, demanding the end of the work-study program, and paying tribute to students who accidentally died while performing it.

On 19 November 2022, about 60 people protested against the presence of the blackface figure of Zwarte Piet in Zaandam (Noord-Holland), denounced as racist. Bystanders threw eggs at the protesters. Police arrested two of these bystanders.

On 16 April 2024, citizens and civil society activists gathered in Zagreb to commemorate the Ahmici massacre in Bosnia and Herzegovina. The activists protested against the Croatian authorities' complicity in this event in 1993 and the lack of consciousness from the current government to condemn this event.
On 11 January 2020, many citizens gathered in front of Prime Minister's office in Tirana, protesting for many reasons, such as poverty, unemployment, and injustice in the country.

On 12 June 2021, leftist Turkish Cypriots of the Left Movement (Sol Hareket) participated in a march in Gonyeli in Northern Nicosia to commemorate the killing of 8 Greek Cypriots by far right Turkish Cypriots on 12 June 1958 and to protest for lasting peace on the island. They were holding placards reading 'confront the past, liberate yourself'.
On 25 September 2020, activists affiliated to the FFF movement gathered for a rally in Siemianowice slaskie, demanding better protection of the climate.

On 6 July 2021, Florence International Airport workers contracted by the Toscana Aeroporti Handling company and USB trade union affiliates gathered outside the airport facility in Florence (Firenze, Toscana) to protest against the company's announced intention to sell its assets and demand guarantees for the future of the workers it employs. The event, which was part of a national day of protest of the sector, was organized by the FILT CGIL, FIT CISL and UILTrasporti (UIL) trade union branches and UGL Toscana.
On 26 May 2020, 12 special law enforcers (BOAs) staged a protest in Den Bosch (Noord-Brabant) to demand more protective equipment in the context of recent violence against BOAs.
On 3 June 2021, members of Danish Association for International Co-operation demonstrated in Copenhagen to demand climate action from the government.

On 14 November 2025, in the evening, under the motto 'Everything starts with words - defend the welfare state', around 50 people staged a protest in front of the town hall in Ludwigsfelde (Brandenburg) against the government's course, warning of a shift to the far-right, social cutbacks, and the AfD's success on social media.

On 31 January 2025, at the call of USB, around 40 precarious workers from tribunals and appeal courts gathered in Bari (Puglia) to protest against their precariousness and to ask for job stabilization.

On 26 September 2022, demonstrators, including activists from the movement Time for Peace protested in front of the Embassy of Sweden in Copenhagen calling on the new Swedish government not to join NATO and to show support and solidarity with Kurdish political activists who sought asylum in Sweden.

On 14 March 2026, at the call of the alliance for Democracy and Civil Courage (Bundnis fur Demokratie und Zivilcourage), around 150 people, including trade union representatives, gathered in front of the cathedral in Speyer (Rheinland-Pfalz) to protest for democracy and social cohesion.

On 23 August 2025, at the call of CiF, activists staged a protest in a bank in L'Ile-Rousse (Corse) to denounce what they described as 'financial colonization.' Participants distributed flyers accusing banks of restricting access to housing loans for Corsican residents, centralizing decisions outside the island, and using local savings to benefit shareholders instead of financing Corsican development. Protesters framed the action as a warning against further dispossession and economic marginalization.

On 5 November 2020, 44 health workers employed at the EFS (French Blood Agency) demonstrated in Brest, at the call of unions (CFDT, CFE-CGC and FO). They demanded the application of the Segur agreements, on health and salary increase, to all health workers, including from the private sector and medico-social centers.

On 13 January 2024, 400-500 activists gathered near the regional headquarters of the national TV in Bydgoszcz, protesting against what they see as politicization of the station by the current government. MPs of the previously ruling Law and Justice party were also present.

On 19 December 2022, 60 cleaning workers of La Candelaria Hospital, summoned by UGT, held a protest in Santa Cruz de Tenerife (Santa Cruz de Tenerife, Canarias) against precariousness and salary cuts amid inflation.
On 18 February 2023, around 20 members of Extinction Rebellion staged a protest and unfurled a banner on the bridge over the Bassin du Commerce in Le Havre, against the local LNG terminal project.

On 21 January 2026, demonstrators, including Kurdish community members, gathered in Orebro to protest a new offensive led by the Syrian military against Kurdish-held areas, and to express solidarity with Rojava and Kurdish civilians.
On 14 March 2026, people demonstrated in Gavle, Gavleborg, to oppose the implementation of stricter migration policies by the government and the recent wave of deportations of teenagers.

On 10 May 2026, in the evening, a large group of residents marched along the seaside in Caulonia (Calabria) in a candlelight demonstration to demand support for those people who suffered the impact and consequences of Storm Harry.

On 12 June 2023, at the call of the 'Citta Sicura' Committee, citizens living in the historic center and shop owners took to the streets of Palermo (Sicilia, Palermo) to demand actions be taken to curb the growing unease of youth and strengthen the presence of police officers to ensure the respect of the law in the area.

On 1 November 2018, 2018 in Montenegrin capital Podgorica hunters protested against the general conditions for hunters in this country, asking the authorities to regulate the legislature concerned with this topic.
On 6 April 2023, around 100 people gathered at the Anger in Erfurt to protest for peace globally.

On 28 November 2020, several hundred people gathered in Helsinki to demand that Finland leave the EU (Fixit) and that the government resign. Several MPs from the Finns Party took part. A counter protest was organized by the anarchist A-group, demanding that public funding/party subsidies be halted to the Finns Party.
On 20 April 2024, GJ affiliates demonstrated in Paris (Ile-de-France) to protest against government policies and demand the resignation of Emmanuel Macron.

On 26 January 2026, demonstrators, including Kurdish community members, demonstrated in Bodo, Nordland, to protest a new offensive led by the Syrian military against Kurdish-held areas, and to express solidarity with Rojava and Kurdish civilians.

On 20 September 2020, an unknown number of students built a mini Moria refugee camp on the Plein in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland) to draw attention to the situation in the Moria refugee camp on the Greek island of Lesbos.

On 1 September 2021, employees of the 'Motorways - Black Sea' gathered in downtown Sofia, Bulgaria, protesting over unpaid BGN 37 million from the state for repairs of a section of the Trakia highway which lead to unpaid salaries.

On 12 February 2021, activists affiliated with the Women's Strike movement and local residents Lublin, protesting against air pollution.
On 6 December 2021, with the support of the CFDT, workers at Constellium company gathered in front of their factory in Montreuil-Juigne to demand for an increase of their salaries.

The event was part of a national day of protest called by RAI employees.

On 17 October 2023, people, summoned by the Por una asistencia pediatrica digna platform, held a protest in Ubrique (Cadiz, Andalucia) to demand better pediatric services. Representatives of PSOE, IU, and PP, such as the mayor of the town Mario Casillas, attended the protest.

On 7 February 2024, ahead of the mass rally against the government's draft bill allowing the establishment of private universities, a small group of students unfurled a banner at Syntagma square, Athens - Central Athens, before they were encircled by DRASI police officers. On 26 June 2023, 8 members of ALG demonstrated and slowed down traffic at Kaiserdamm in Berlin - Charlottenburg-Wilmersdorf to call for climate protection.

On 1 July 2020, trade union SI Cobas staged a protest outside a logistics company's branch in Modena (Modena, Emilia-Romagna) against the dismissal of two employees, caused by an argument between the two.

On 9 March 2025, around 20 residents of Novogradska Street protested outside the former military barracks 'Jakub Kuburovic' in Belgrade - Zemun. On 2 February 2023, a dozen parents of students gathered for a protest in front of their school in La Ferriere-sur-Risle, against the decision to close a kindergarten class.

On 13 November 2022, 100 people, including members of the collectives 'La Deroute des routes' and 'SOS Oulala', gathered in Grabels, to demonstrate against the construction of the Montpellier road project LIEN (liaison intercantonale d'evitement du nord).

On 24 January 2026, demonstrators, including Kurdish community members, gathered in Odense, Syddanmark, to protest a new offensive led by the Syrian military against Kurdish-held areas, and to express solidarity with Rojava and Kurdish civilians.

On 6 May 2019, in Croatian city of Split, a clash occurred between the war veterans commemorating a rally against the Yugoslav army 28 years ago, and two men demonstrating over the death of a young Macedonian soldier during that same demonstration.

On 8 February 2025, at the call of the Alliance Against the Right, including the SPD, The Left, The Greens, cultural organizations and the Refugees Forum (Fluchtlingsforum), around 4,000 people staged a protest in Lubeck (Schleswig-Holstein) against far-right ideologies. On 28 March 2023, members of CSIF held a protest in Granada (Andalucia) against the low compensations public employees receive for spending the night away from their residence for work reasons and to demand solutions.

On 14 January 2023, about 70 people gathered for a march in Berlin - Charlottenburg-Wilmersdorf, demanding higher tolerance and support for people with physical disabilities or mental health problems.

On 5 September 2020, around 50 people protested in Eschwege with a human chain for peace and disarmament on the occasion of the 'Anti-War Day'. The protest was organised by the DGB and the Peace Plenum.

On 6 September 2025, residents protested in Olleros de Tera (Castilla y Leon) in support of a local bar owner who was arrested for stabbing a man during an alleged robbery. Protesters demanded his prompt release and more protection measures in rural areas.

On 25 September 2024, around 600 residents held a protest in Montalban (Aragon) in defense of public health and denounced the lack of health professionals in the health centers of this rural area. Protesters blocked the road.

Around 1 February 2020 (as reported), a week earlier a group of parents gathered outside of a school in Bettystown, Co. Meath, to demand the need for better school services.

Police arrested six people from both sides for incidents such as setting off flares, breaching police lines, and spitting on an officer.

On 29 June 2021, between 550-600 citizens protested in the Tetuan district in Madrid - Tetuan (Madrid) against the closure of the Villaamil health centre.

Pro-Gest packaging manufacture workers gathered, with the support of trade unions, outside their factory's gates in Altopascio (Lucca, Toscana) to protest against the company's management. Workers were joined by the town's mayor and a center-right municipal councilor and mayoral candidate.

On 30 June 2020, around 300 people staged a protest in Brasschaat against the imminent establishment of school project De Kaart in their neighbourhood.

On 1 May 2020, people from the far right gathered in Erfurt for a protest. People from the far left gathered for a counter-protest. The exact reasons for the demonstrations were not reported.

The protesters questioned the way police handled the disappearance of migrant women workers, mostly Filipinos, and decried 'sexist, misogynist and racist' attitudes. On 3 July 2020, members of KTAMS rallied in Northern Nicosia outside the headquarters of a bank to protest against its practices.

On 28 July 2023, CGIL and UIL representatives staged a protest in front of the Prefecture in Messina (Messina, Sicilia) to demand increased health and safety in construction sites and any other workplace.
On 24 September 2022, around 200 Carrefour workers gathered in front of the supermarket in Antibes on the occasion of their strike, calling for a reevaluation of their salaries.

The event was happening ahead of the Conservatives party conference in Birmingham on 2 October. The rally was part of a national day of protest organized by the campaign.

Masaryk Square in Plzen (Plzen-mesto) with banners, Czech flags, whistles and drums, then marched about one kilometer along Klatovska street to Peace Square and to the Czech Radio Plzen studio, organized by the Million Moments for Democracy association under the slogan 'Hands off the media'. Czech Radio employees displayed a heart and 'Thank you' sign on the facade. Speakers warned that the Czech Republic was moving towards eastern authoritarian models and demanded the withdrawal of a government bill transferring the financing of Czech Television and Czech Radio from license fees to the state budget.

On 19 June 2021, around 200 pro-Palestine protesters demonstrated in Lausanne in solidarity with Palestinians. Protesters called on authorities to take sanctions against the State of Israel.

On 17 September 2021, biologists protested in Madrid, demanding greater professional recognition. They protested being considered technicians at hospitals instead of health personnel - which positions them in a more precarious labour situation.

On 17 March 2023, Fridays for Future activists demonstrated outside of the city hall in Malmo to draw attention to environmental problems and to demand action against climate change.

Protesters displayed banners and attempted to negotiate the bear's release with the owner, who refused them entry and maintained that his facility meets all national legal standards. Following a report from the owner regarding an unauthorized gathering on his property, police intervened and escorted the activists away from the private premises to a nearby road. A veterinarian from the activist group was eventually permitted to inspect the bear's condition before the protesters departed.

On 28 January 2025, farmers with about 10 tractors gathered along the Aurelia Road near Torrimpietra (Lazio) as part of a national demonstration to protest against the growing crisis in the sector. Protesters asked for more support and criticized the government for its lack of concrete actions following last year's demonstrations.
On 21 March 2021, people demonstrated in Eindhoven (Noord-Brabant) against racism on the occasion of UN International Day Against Racism and Discrimination.
On 25 February 2023, people gathered in Valence to protest against Russia's war efforts and show solidarity with Ukraine, on the one-year anniversary of the conflict.

On 8 January 2022, about 30 activists, including members of ORP and representatives of environmental groups, gathered near Huta Szklana, protesting against destruction of natural environment in their neighborhood.

On 4 June 2023, a group of people, called by the Platform in Defense of a Decent Health of the Basic Health Zone of Tabara, staged a protest in Tabara (Zamora, Castilla y Leon) demanding better health care services, including employing more health care professionals so that the health centers operate 24/7 and offer specialist patient care.

On 18 November 2023, people participated in a pro-Palestine protest in Koln (Nordrhein-Westfalen) under the motto 'Frieden fur den Nahen Osten' (Peace for the Near East) against what they claimed to be a one-sided stance of the German political class and the media in the Middle East conflict, and to show solidarity with the Palestinian population in Gaza.

On 9 April 2025, in the afternoon, at the call of MD and four other groups including Animal Equality, around 100 activist and demonstrators gathered outside the Zaantheater in Zaandam (Noord-Holland), near the Ahold Delhaize shareholders' meeting, to protest the unaffordability of organic food and rising CO2 emissions, accusing Ahold of making sustainable food a luxury by overpricing organics, and criticizing the company for using profits to reward shareholders instead of investing in climate goals.
On 31 January 2021, More Europe and Italian Radicals activists gathered outside the Russian Consulate in Florence to demand the release of Navalny, who was arrested by the Russian authorities.

Around 17 April 2023, train drivers demonstrated in front of the central station in Stockholm to oppose the municipality's decision to replace around 400 train hosts with CCTV cameras and in support of the ongoing strike.

On 8 March 2022, on the occasion of International Women's Day, Di Marzio Michetti high school students, including a member of the Ukrainian community, and teachers gathered for a 'flash mob' protest in Pescara (Pescara, Abruzzo) to defend women's rights, protest against the war in Ukraine and send a message of solidarity to all Ukrainian women.
On 26 June 2021, citizens, including LGBT activists, staged a pride parade in Talavera de la Reina (Toledo). They demanded greater protection for transgender rights.

On 24 June 2025, a group of people, led by an independent MP, protested at the Franciscan Square (Ferenciek tere) in Budapest, Hungary, calling against the so-called transparency law and the restrictions on the right to assemble. The MP also supported the upcoming Pride march, labelling it as an example of endangered freedom of speech and expression, and also condemned the persisting strong anti-Ukrainian propaganda of the current government. After this, the protesters marched to the Corvinus Square in Budapest - XIII., commemorating the suppression of protests in 1956.
On 9 July 2022, more than 2,000 people, including members of the LGBT+ community, demonstrated in Wurzburg for LGBT+ rights, equality, and tolerance. They gathered on Christopher Street Day (CSD).

On 17 January 2025, around 20 citizens protested in Vranje to show their support for students who have been occupying their faculties nationwide, demanding accountability for the loss of 15 lives following the collapse of a concrete canopy at the train station in Novi Sad, ultimately blaming corruption for this tragic event. The protesters also observed 15 minutes of silence as part of the 'Serbia, Stop' campaign, with an aim to honor the 15 victims and voice their demands.

On 21 September 2023, at the call of the Uniterre and BBK (Bernisch Bauerliches Komitee) farmers' unions, 5 farmers gathered outside Elsa Group's headquarters in Estavayer-le-Lac (Fribourg) to protest against Elsa Group's decision to lower the price of milk.

On 17 October 2025, hundreds of secondary and university students gathered in Palermo (Sicilia) in memory of a student killed in the Olivella area, and to demand greater safety in nightlife and across the city.

On 18 June 2024, members of ACORN held a protest outside the house of a mom with four kids in Bristol (England) to protest against the bailiff's plans to evict her and her family. The bailiff left as protesters blocked access to the house.

On 7 March 2025, students, actors, and citizens gathered in front of the National Theatre in Leskovac in support of the actors on strike, who are aligning their demands with students to seek accountability for the loss of 15 lives following the collapse of a concrete canopy at the train station in Novi Sad. The protest marks the first day of the 'general strike', where workers and consumers across Serbia halted their activities to support the students' demands.

On 1 July 2020, hundreds of people, including members of National Union of Rail, Maritime and Transport Workers, gathered outside the Home Office in Glasgow for an anti-racism protest organized by Stand Up To Racism, demanding rights for refugees.

On 31 May 2025, activists from the Reclaim the Future movement and Extinction Rebellion associated group held a sit-in protest outside of the Swedish Social Democrats' national congress venue in Gothenburg (Goteborg), Vastra Gotaland, to demand wealth taxes for climate and welfare, and to call attention to the perceived party's lack of focus on the climate crisis.

On 21 June 2022, around 150 public transport workers protested in front of the Serbian presidency in Belgrade - Stari Grad, demanding improved working conditions, collective agreement and increased salaries
On 18 July 2023, around 11 Animal Save activists held a vigil outside of a meat processing facility near Boras, Vastra Gotaland, to oppose animal rights violations and to promote animal welfare.
On 1 November 2023, around 100 people gathered in Montreuil (Ile-de-France), to denounce the Kasparian-Berge law, which facilitates the eviction of squatters.

On 30 May 2021, several thousand people organized by In the Name of the Family, marched through Zagreb, Croatia, demanding a ban on abortions. A group of counter-protesters stood along the march route, demanding abortion be kept safe and legal.

On 11 February 2023, about 600 people took to the streets in Genova (Genova, Liguria) to protest against the eviction of the self-managed social center Zapata. Left-wing politicians took part in the demonstration.

On 28 June 2022, people demonstrated in front of the Parliament of Norway in Oslo to denounce the recent shooting outside a gay bar in central Oslo and to call for the respect of the rights of members of the LGBTQ+ community. Members from the Communist Party of Norway (NKP), the Socialist Youth (SU); the Young Greens of Norway, the Red Party and the Red Youth took part in the event, among others.

Around 21 September 2022 (as reported), an unknown number of people staged a protest in front of the Palace of Justice in Brussels - Ville de Bruxelles to denounce the acquittal of the police officers who were involved in the fatal pursuit of a couple on a motorcycle in 2017.

On 13 April 2025, activists from Extinction Rebellion, Alton Climate Action Network, Farnborough Noise Group and the Friends of the Earth held a protest and blocked one of the entrances to Farnborough Airport in Farnborough (England) against plans for airport's expansion, and to highlight the impact of private jets and frequent flyers on the environment.

On 14 April 2021, around 40 people, including immigrant families (from Kosovo, Albania, and other countries), members from different organizations (RESF, FSU, FCPE), protested in Toulouse to call on authorities to grant legal status to school children and undocumented migrants. This protest is linked to the movement 'Let's lift the lockdown on their rights'.

On 12 April 2023, as part of a spotaneous day of strike, in the morning, people, including students and SUD affiliates, blocked the Lille 3 University in Lille to oppose the passing of the pension reform bill.

On 21 February 2025, activists gathered for a rally in Liptovsky Mikulas, commemorating the 7th anniversary of the politically motivated murder of Jan Kuciak and Martina Kusnirova and demanding proper investigation and punishment for perpetrators. They also condemned the current political representation led by the Smer party, in particular what they see as anti-democratic and anti-western attitudes of the PM Robert Fico.
On 26 January 2025, several dozen Belarusian activists gathered for a rally near their embassy in Prague, protesting against unfair and unfree election of the president in Minsk.

On 2 September 2024, hundreds to thousands of students and teachers protested in front of the Ministry of the Interior in Budapest - V, District 5, against restrictions on cell phone use in schools and the dismissal of the principal of Madach High School, demanding his reinstatement. The protesters also expressed broader frustration with systemic issues in the education system, including perceived repressive measures and the erosion of educational standards. The event was attended by members of the National Assembly of Hungary, including a Jobbik member, Hungarian Socialist Party members, Peter Magyar from the Tisza Party and the European Parliament.

On 25 November 2021, hundreds of people marched through Bristol for the Reclaim The Night march to protest against gender-based violence and gender inequality. A Bristol University student organized the protest.

On 2 February 2023, 7 municipal councilors (civic lists), as well as the head of the Council, occupied the municipal council room in Pachino (Siracusa, Sicilia) to protest against the precarious conditions of the local health system and the shortage of doctors at the town's hospital, which resulted in the death of a 38-year-old farmer a few days prior.

On 29 June 2023, overnight, dozens of rioters threw mortar fireworks, set on fire a truck and several trash bins in Nice (Provence-Alpes-Cote d'Azur). No fatalities nor injuries were reported. The event was part of a national wave of riots and demonstrations denouncing police violence and demanding justice in the wake of the shooting and subsequent death of 17-year-old Nahel M. by a police officer in Nanterre on 27 June 2023.

On 21 January 2025, citizens in Kula protested after a local activist from the 'Bravo' citizens' movement was assaulted the day before for putting up posters supporting nationwide protests in response to the tragic deaths of 15 people following the collapse of a concrete canopy at the Novi Sad train station. The protesters demanded that authorities identify the assailants within 72 hours.

On 28 June 2020, several dozen students of the Haute Ecole Francisco Ferrer staged a protest in front of the school in Brussels - Ville de Bruxelles to denounce alleged mismanagement by its personnel.

On 11 July 2022, at the call of the health branch of CGT, dozens of health workers demonstrated in front of the Regional Health Agency in Marseille to denounce the state of the region's public hospitals.
On 14 March 2025, Fridays For Future activists demonstrated in Malmo, Skane, to draw attention to environmental issues and to demand action against climate change.

On 28 January 2025, farmers with 10 tractors gathered in Migliarino Pisano (Toscana), near the exit for the motorway A11, as part of a national demonstration to protest against the growing crisis in the sector. Protesters asked for more support and criticized the government for its lack of concrete actions following last year's demonstrations. Representatives of Coapi, RA, and CIA participated in the protest.

On 22 April 2023, 70 people gathered in the streets of Rennes before heading to Charles-De-Gaulle Square to oppose the construction of a new pastry factory industrial site in the area by the Le Duff group.

On 22 March 2026, dozens of people gathered in Milano - Municipio 9 (Lombardia) to express their support to Palestine and show solidarity with pro-Palestine activists who are currently facing trial on charges of aiding terrorist groups. Activists also emphasized the importance of continuing support for Gaza, highlighting the need for humanitarian aid and backing the new Global Sumud Flotilla mission.

On 27 April 2025, at the call of PACMA, around 2,000 people marched in Sevilla (Andalucia) to protest against bullfighting, calling for Spain to follow other countries in banning the practice. The demonstration ended in front of the Maestranza bullring and included symbolic imagery denouncing violence against animals.
On 5 June 2024, an Extinction Rebeliion associated group staged a sit-in protest in Orebro to call for action against climate change and to raise awareness about environmental issues.

On 20 September 2021, C&P workers gathered outside their company in the Isca area of Chiaromonte (Potenza, Basilicata) to protest against the stopping of the working activities imposed by the judicial authorities which has continued since July 21st. Mayors from the area took part in the demonstration.

On 15 February 2025, around 1,500 people gathered for a protest organized by 'Tuttlingen is colorful' in Tuttlingen (Baden-Wurttemberg) against far-right ideology and activity, while recording a lip-sync video to the song 'Say No' by Konstantin Wecker to support protests against fascism, racism, patriarchy, and the AfD.

On 23 October 2025, people demonstrated outside of the Town Hall in Kerteminde, Syddanmark, to oppose the proposed expansion of Odense Harbour, raising concerns about its potential negative impact on the local environment and the local community.
On 22 December 2023, around 150 people gathered in Pau (Nouvelle-Aquitaine) to protest against the passing of the new immigration law, which they deemed xenophobic and unfair to immigrants.

On 1 June 2023, around 50 members of the platform of families of public education 'Escuela de calor', with the support of the Educational Green Tide and the Student Union, held a protest before the City Council in Sevilla (Andalucia) against the high temperatures in the classrooms and the lack of air conditioning. Members of For Andalusia and AA took part in the demonstration.

On 23 April 2021, around 300 persons, including members of the CGT union and independent professionals of the cultural sector, demonstrated in Clermont-Ferrand. They denounced precariousness and demonstrated against a reform of the unemployment insurance.

On 13 March 2022, a group of people protested in front of the Russian Embassy in Vilnius, Lithuania calling against the abduction of the mayor of Melitopol in Ukraine by the Russian Military during the Russian invasion of Ukraine.

On 21 March 2026, at the call of the Collective of Support for Migrants from Goelo (Collectif de Soutien aux Migrants du Goelo) and LDH, around 100 people gathered in Paimpol (Bretagne) to protest against all forms of discrimination on the occasion of the International Day for the Elimination of Racial Discrimination.

On 18 January 2025, at the call of the UK Women's March, women marched in Glasgow (Scotland) as part of a nationwide Women's March protesting increasing reports of violence against women. The protest occurred just days before Donald Trump's inauguration as President of the United States and featured signs condemning his presidency, the pro-life movement, and transphobia.

On 1 May 2021, about 100 nationalist activists, including members of the ONR movement, gathered for a rally in Bialystok, protesting against liberalism and wild capitalism. Law enforcers and a representative of a local municipality ordered them to disperse due to sanitary restrictions.

On 26 March 2021, Fridays For Future activists staged a protest in front of the City Hall in Jonkoping to draw attention to environmental problems and to demand action against climate change. No students were present based on the report.
On 23 October 2020, about 200 activists gathered in Minsk Mazowiecki for a rally, protesting against proposed restrictions of abortions in Poland.
On 15 May 2021, about 100 activists gathered for a rally in Prague, declaring their support for Israel during the ongoing conflict.
On 31 August 2025, SNS supporters gathered in Bolec neighborhood of Grocka to express support for the government and oppose student-led protests and blockades.
On 9 July 2020, activists affiliated to the movement Democratic Action gathered in Warsaw, protesting against the current president and presidential candidate.

On 12 July 2023, RTE staff (Irish public service broadcaster) held a protest rally at the RTE headquarters in Cork (Cork) after the revelation of the payments controversy to Irish broadcaster Ryan Tubridy. The protest was organized by the National Union of Journalists and SIPTU.
On 24 August 2022, several hundred people assembled on the Erasmus bridge in Rotterdam to celebrate the Ukrainian national day and demand peace in Ukraine. People with Ukrainian roots were present.

On 10 November 2021, around 30 asylum seekers from Sierra Leone protested and camped in front of the immigration authorities' headquarters in Munchen (Maxvorstadt district) against deportation and for legal status.
On 23 August 2020, around 1000 citizens protested in Aguilar de Campoo (Palencia), demanding to stop the installation project of fourteen slaughterhouses in the region.

On 20 March 2024, Last Generation activists gathered outside the offices of the energy and oil company TotalEnergies in Berlin - Mitte (Berlin), while holding a banner saying 'Stop EACOP-pipeline'. The event aimed to oppose the planned East African Crude Oil Pipeline (EACOP), set to connect two oil fields in Uganda with a new oil terminal in Tanzania. Demonstrators cited environmental concerns.
On 27 June 2020, in the afternoon, demonstrators of the CGT union and LFI gathered in Saintes. They protested against police brutality and demanded a better recognition of health workers.

On 13 February 2024, 90 farmers blocked the A6 road in San Vicente del Palacio (Castilla y Leon) to demonstrate. The event was part of a nationwide farmers' demonstration movement against the ratification of the EU's free-trade agreements until partner third countries comply with the EU's agricultural standards, and in favor of fair production prices for Spanish farmers, relief measures to offset the consequences of droughts and of the import of agricultural products from Ukraine, as well as better working and social conditions in their sector.

On 28 March 2025, people gathered in San Sebastian (Pais Vasco) to demonstrate against the eviction of an occupied self-managed center, which took place on 19 March. Demonstrators vandalized local businesses and set garbage containers on fire and spray-painted walls insulting and accusing the City Council and Mayor Eneko Goia of being classist and racist, which led to police intervention.
On 19 April 2020, tens of residents held a protest at three locations in Sofia against the coronavirus lockdown measures, which led to losing their jobs and income.

On 19 November 2025, at the call of CCOO, several people, including Turkish nationals, protested outside the Camp Nou stadium in Barcelona - Les Corts (Cataluna) to demand protection measures for the undocumented migrant workers who were laid off after a labor inspection. Protesters called for their readmission, citing their vulnerability.

On 28 June 2023, overnight, rioters set fire to the 'Restos du Coeur' and 4 other buildings, some of which hosted municipal services, in Vernon. The event was part of a national wave of riots and demonstrations denouncing police violence and demanding justice in the wake of the shooting and subsequent death of 17-year-old Nahel M. by a police officer in Nanterre on 27 June 2023.

On 24 May 2025, at the call of XR, activists distributed free clothing and informed passersby in Heerlen (Limburg) to protest the fast fashion industry's environmental and human rights abuses. The action, which took place in several Dutch cities, highlighted issues such as pollution, overproduction, CO2 emissions, water waste, and labor exploitation. Protesters called for radical change, demanding the end of overproduction, fair treatment of workers, and the promotion of sustainable alternatives.

On 28 June 2025, at the call of CP, farmers gathered and planted flowers in Cahors (Occitanie) to protest against the Duplomb Law, which aimed to legalize the use of certain previously banned pesticides, citing their potential environmental impact and health risks for both farmers and consumers.

On 28 November 2023, farmers and Core in Fronte affiliates gathered in Vivario (Corse) to express solidarity with local farmers who are confronted with financial hardship and difficult working conditions. The protesters also called for more state support for farmers.

On 23 September 2021, answering the call of SUD union, around 100 workers in school demonstrated at the Capitol place in Toulouse. They denounced their working conditions since the start of the academic year.

On 13 March 2023, striking NHS junior doctors represented by BMA formed a picket line outside Hospitals in Bristol over a pay dispute and working conditions. The event was part of 72-hour national industrial action.

On 24 October 2025, at 6:30 pm, 300 residents, business owners, workers, women, and representatives of local associations gathered at the Porta Cauana in Napoli (Campania) to protest violence against women and criminality and staged a candlelight procession to demand safety and foster the relaunch of the neighborhood following the rape of a resident. A municipal councilor (PD) participated in the demonstration.
On 1 December 2022, farmers blocked the Struma highway in Simitli to protest against the low buying prices of the produce and meat products imposed by the European Union.

On 14 December 2024, a few Extinction Rebellion activists protested outside the ING office at Hereplein in Groningen (Groningen). The protest aimed to encourage ING customers to switch banks, criticizing ING for its significant investments in fossil fuels and poor human rights record. Activists cited research showing ING's continued investment in coal, oil, and gas, and referenced an Amnesty International report on the bank's human rights practices. As part of the protest, they offered a service to help people switch banks.

On 28 March 2021, between 200 and 250 environmental activists protested in Cahors to call on the government to implement concrete measures to tackle climate change. Protesters denounced that the climate and resilience bill was not stringent enough to meet the 2030 greenhouse gas emission reduction target. They also called for the 149 proposals from the Citizens Convention for Climate to be implemented. The event was part of a national day of protest called by Greenpeace, Friends of the Earth, International Movement ATD Fourth World, Attac, CARE, CCFD-Terre Solidaire (Catholic Committee against hunger and for development), XR, L214, FAGE, France Nature Environnement (French Nature Environment), Generations Futures (Future Generations), LDH, LPO - Ligue pour la protection des oiseaux (League for the Protection of Birds), Notre affaire a tous (Everyone's Business), OXFAM, SDN, EELV, Generation Ecologie (Ecology Generation), CFDT, and PS, before consideration by parliament of the government's climate and resilience bill, which they criticized.

On 15 February 2025, at the call of the 'Antisiko' action alliance, around 1,400 people gathered in Munchen (Bayern) to against the Munich security conference. The protest march started at Stachus and proceeded towards Marienplatz and it was supported by various left-wing groups. 'Palestina Speaks Munich' was present. This protest became partly a pro-Palestinian rally, while still with a focus on voicing opposition to military escalation, especially NATO actions and arms shipments, calling for peace and an end to violence.

On 8 March 2024, several dozen farmers and ranchers with 5 tractors held a protest at the premises of the Ministry of Agriculture in Valladolid (Castilla y Leon) and blocked the street. The event was part of a nationwide farmers' demonstration movement against the ratification of the EU's free-trade agreements until partner third countries comply with the EU's agricultural standards, and in favor of fair production prices for Spanish farmers, relief measures to offset the consequences of droughts and of the import of agricultural products from Ukraine, as well as better working and social conditions in their sector.
On 19 November 2019, teachers, students and their parents shut down the school in Dali for 45 minutes and protested against pollution caused by the nearby asphalt plant.
On 24 February 2023, Kvinnostrejk movement activists demonstrated in Falun, Dalarna, to oppose violence against women and in support of women's rights.

On 28 June 2023, overnight, rioters set fire to the town hall and a cultural center in Montigny-les-Cormeilles (Ile-de-France). The event was part of a national wave of riots and demonstrations denouncing police violence and demanding justice in the wake of the shooting and subsequent death of 17-year-old Nahel M. by a police officer in Nanterre on 27 June 2023.

On 7 October 2023, at the call of Comite International de Defense des Femmes Afghanes, Association de Solidarite a Tous les Immigres (ASTI), around 50 people, including students and municipal councilor Jean-Philippe Grand (EELV), gathered in Orleans (Centre-Val de Loire) to call for the reception of Afghan women.

On 7 December 2025, students, professors and citizens protested and marched in Novi Sad, South Backa region, in support of a professor and provincial MP from the Movement of Free Citizens who is under house arrest after six PSG and Bravo activists were arrested ahead of a major protest in Belgrade on March 15.

On 7 March 2026, at the call of the Coordination of Sardinian Committees (Coordinamento dei Comitati Sardi), around 1,000 people gathered in Cagliari (Sardegna) to demonstrate against the crisis in Sardinia's public healthcare system. The protest targeted long waiting lists for specialist care, cuts to medical staff, and the growing difficulties faced by hospitals.

On 28 September 2023, at the call of Deutsche Tierschutzbund (German Animal Welfare Association), people demonstrated in front of the Federal Chancellery in Berlin - Mitte to denounce their precarious situation. They called for more financial support from the government, and a new animal protection law.

On 28 November 2024, local council members from Pazardzhik protested after one of their colleagues was called in for questioning, claiming that the police investigation is interfering with their regular day-to-day duties and that the entire process was launched by another member of the council for personal benefit.

On 1 May 2026, people marched in Gothenburg (Goteborg), Vastra Gotaland, to mark Labor Day and show support for workers' rights. Among other things, the activists expressed opposition to the gender pay gap and to violations of workers' rights in workplaces. Members from the Social Democratic Party (S), the Swedish Trade Union Confederation (LO) participated in the event, among others.

On 26 September 2024, animal rights activists held a twelve-hour vigil outside the Tonnies slaughterhouse in Rheda-Wiedenbruck (Nordrhein-Westfalen), aiming to raise awareness about the treatment of animals in slaughterhouses by displaying images of sad pigs and protesting for a more radical movement against such facilities.

On 2 May 2020, members of the newly-born movement Tricolor Masks gathered in Giordano square in Foggia (Foggia, Puglia) to protest against the 'healthcare dictatorship' allegedly imposed by the Italian government to contain the spread of coronavirus. The event was part of a national day of protest which occurred in 66 other localities across the country.

On 13 December 2025, residents of Smolyan protested in the Ustovo district against the construction of a photovoltaic power plant. Organized by the initiative committee 'For Ustovo,' demonstrators opposed deforestation and demanded the cancellation of a long-term land lease approved by the municipal council.

On 21 December 2025, vegan animal rights group Hungarian Animal Rights Corps (HARC) demonstrated in front of the Franciscan church at Ferenciek Square in Budapest - V (District 5), displaying a Christmas tree decorated with fake animal carcasses and bloody ornaments. Protesters distributed brochures and spoke through loudspeakers criticizing the meat and dairy industries, arguing that celebrating Christmas with animal slaughter contradicts the holiday's message of love.
On 25 October 2019, a day after the development bill was voted in parliament, students rallied outside the Ministry of Education in Athens to protest against the education reforms.
On 29 August 2020, around 160 animal rights activists protested in Kellinghusen in front of a Tonnies slaughterhouse for an end to slaughtering animals and against the meat industry.
On 11 June 2020, around 200 people, including Antifa activists, protested in Ludwigsburg against racism after a young black man was attacked by two racists in Egolsheim.

On 6 February 2024, about 300 Stellantis workers employed at the Mirafiori plant and representatives of FIOM CGIL demonstrated outside the plant in Torino (Piemonte) to protest against the reduction in production and the extension of the redundancy payment program decided by the company's management.

On 27 May 2026, at the call of Polish Teachers' Union (Zwiazek Nauczycielstwa Polskiego), NSZZ and Workers' Initiative (Inicjatywa Pracownicza), researchers, doctoral students and academic staff from across Poland protested in front of the Polish parliament in Warsaw (Mazowieckie), demanding increased funding for science and higher education.

On 6 March 2025, at the call of Ver.di, around 100 employees from the social and educational services, as well as healthcare workers, staged a protest in Luneburg (Niedersachsen) to protest for higher wages and better working conditions. The protest was part of a wider strike and protest movement in the public sector amid ongoing negotiations.
On 13 June 2021, members of AnimaNaturalis gathered in Valencia to protest against bullfighting. Protesters also demanded to stop giving subsidies to the bullfighting sector.

On 23 February 2023, members and supporters of the Democratic Party protested in front of the parliament in Tirana, demanding the resignation of Prime Minister Edi Rama and claiming that his resignation would finally lead to democratic reform and more transparency in the country.

On 13 April 2024, at the call of 'Students Against the Right' (Studies gegen Rechts), people, including Grannies Against the Right, participated in a protest in Bremen (Bremen) for diversity and democracy and against discrimination.
On 22 November 2021, students gathered outside Emili-Romagna Region headquarters in Bologna at the call of UDU to protest against the underfunding of public education.
On 5 February 2020, the OGB organized a protest in Vienna in support of the social economy and better working conditions.

On 25 May 2023, hundreds of workers in nursing and residential homes and in the home care and disability care sectors held a protest march in Utrecht, to demand higher wages and better working conditions. Among protesters were affiliates of the FNV union.

On 4 May 2022, hundreds of cab drivers took part in a demonstration, which saw cabs drive slowly around West Bromwich town center and the surrounding area. They demonstrated against the Sandwell charge for badges.
On 3 July 2021, around 1,500 environmental and climate activists protested in Bochum for more climate action. The protest was co-organized by the BUND.

On 22 May 2025, around 1000 people demonstrated outside of the Finnish Parliament in Helsinki to call on the government to take concrete action in response to the situation in Gaza, including recognizing Palestine and ending arms trade with Israel. The event was organized by Amnesty International.
On 14 October 2019, hundreds of citizens of Bor, Serbia, gathered in front of a mining company in that city, blaming it for air pollution.

On 9 June 2020, activists gathered for a rally in Chlumec nad Cidlinou, protesting against some particular steps taken by the government and related to the coronavirus pandemic, but also against the attitude of the PM and the president towards China or the media of public service. The rally was organized by the movement Million Moments for Democracy.

On 2 June 2023, Kosovo Serb protesters gathered in front of the municipality of Gracanica to demand that the Albanian mayors that won in the local elections that they boycotted not take their offices, since they claim they do not represent them. The protests mark an escalation in tensions between the two communities in Kosovo, after months of simmering tensions in the Serb-majority area of the country.

On 23 April 2021, around 50 demonstrators, including independent professionals of the cultural sector and precarious professionals, gathered in front of the Hippodrome in Douai at the call of the CGT union. They demonstrated against a reform of the unemployment insurance.
On 23 May 2024, an unknown number of Flemish Interest members organized a protest action in Itterbeek (Vlaanderen) to denounce the urban development of Dilbeek.
On 13 May 2022, protests took place in front of the state inspectorate for environmental protection in Skopje to raise awareness about the pollution being caused by the Paper Mill plant in Kochani.

On 20 May 2025, people demonstrated outside of the Danish Parliament in Copenhagen to protest against a proposed law to raise the retirement age to 70 years. Representatives of various trade unions, including the United Federation of Danish Workers (3F), the Construction, Land and Environmental Workers' Union (BJMF) and the Association of Child and Youth Educators (BUPL) participated in the event, among others.

On 18 September 2025, between 2,000 and 4,500 people, including union delegates, demonstrated in La Roche-sur-Yon (Pays de la Loire). The march began at 14:00 from Boulevard Sully, proceeding through Rue Monge, Boulevard des Etablieres, Boulevard des Flaneries, and returning to Boulevard Sully. Protesters, many wearing union colors, denounced wage freezes, growing precarity, and the distribution of public funds to companies without conditions, while also raising broader concerns such as democracy, youth prospects, and the situation in Palestine. The event was part of a nationwide strike and demonstration day called by CFDT, CGT, FO, CFE-CGC, CFTC, UNSA, FSU, and SUD to oppose the government's draft 2026 budget, condemn austerity measures affecting public services and welfare, and denounce the perceived erosion of wages and social protections.
On 23 October 2020, 12 local students gathered for a Fridays for Future protest in Tartu, demanding more decisive action by governments in the face of climate change.

On 9 May 2026, under the motto 'We've had enough! Stop the suffering of animals in Poland', animal rights activists staged a protest in Katowice (Slaskie), demanding stronger animal protection laws, including mandatory microchipping, free sterilization and castration programs, stricter penalties for animal abuse and a ban on chaining animals. The event was part of a wider protest action called by KARUNA Foundation - People for Animals and Coalition for Sterilizing Stray Animals (Koalicja Kastrujemy Bezdomnosc) demanding accessible and free animal sterilization programs.

On 1 May 2025, workers organized by PEO marked International Labor Day and protested for improved labor rights, higher wages, affordable housing and renewed efforts for peace and the reunification of Cyprus. They rallied, held speeches and marched in Pafos.

Participants sang songs, held signs with pro-democracy messages, and called on people to vote in the upcoming Parliament election to protect democratic values.

On 8 March 2024, on the occasion of International Women's Day, around 400 people, called by Feminists Action (Accio Feminista), gathered in Andorra la Vella (Andorra), against gender based violence and demanding sexual and reproductive rights.

On 29 January 2022, residents of Herceg Novi protested against the privatization and possible transfer of the local public hospital to another location, claiming that it is an essential institution for both the locals and visitors.

On 15 June 2024, protesters gathered in Plovdiv to voice their opposition to the Pride parade in the country, advocating for traditional families and claiming that traditional family values are being threatened by the LGBTQ+ community and other groups.
On 24 February 2023, around 100 people gathered in Lulea, Norrbotten, to show support and solidarity with Ukraine on one year anniversary of Russia's invasion.

On 9 December 2022, Roma demonstrators blocked the highway at Zevgolateio, revolting against police violence, after a police officer shot and critically injured a Roma teenager during a car chase near Thessaloniki 4 days earlier. No clashes were reported.

On 30 January 2022, citizens, including AnimaNaturalis representatives, protested against the animal protection law draft in Plaza Mayor in Madrid - Centro. They demanded greater protection for hunting dogs.

On 7 August 2024, hundreds of anti-racism protesters formed a human shield outside a targeted church that hosts an immigration advice center in Liverpool (England) against the anti-migration and Islamophobic riots across England amid the fear of far-right demonstrations near the immigration centers. Protesters held signs such as 'Refugees welcome' and 'Nans against Nazis'. Similar peaceful protests were held across the country. SUTR organized the protest. The event is part of a wave of gatherings and violence that occurred across the country and was triggered by the stabbing of children in Southport on 29 July 2024 and the disinformation campaign on social media about the suspect of the attack being a refugee.
On 27 August 2022, around 400 people took part in a Pride march in Savonlinna, protesting for LGBT and human rights.

On 9 January 2024, around 30 One Voice affiliates gathered outside the Marineland wildlife park in Antibes (Provence-Alpes-Cote d'Azur) to protest against the transfer of 6 orcas to Japan, which they considered animal cruelty.
On 3 October 2020, residents of Mostar, Bosnia and Herzegovina, protested against the local landfill, claiming it does not meet environmental standards.

On 21 February 2026, around 30 people, including Ukrainian refugees, gathered in front of the Russian Consulate in Strasbourg (Grand Est) to express continued solidarity with Ukraine ahead of the fourth anniversary of Russia's 2022 invasion. This event was part of a broader wave of demonstrations commemorating the fourth year since the start of the war in Ukraine on 24 February 2022 and calling for an end to Russian aggression.

On 20 January 2022, farmers gathered for demonstrative rides around Prerov with their machines. They were protesting against a new system of funding of agriculture proposed by the government and demanding negotiations.
On 23 April 2022, around 50 people staged a protest in Maastricht in support of the Palestinian people.

On 15 December 2024, around 16 people, including members of the Kurdish Cultural Center, marched from the train station to Erlon Square in Reims (Grand Est) to support the civilian populations in the Rojava region of Syria amid violent clashes between Kurdish militias and the Syrian army in Northeastern Syria. Participants condemned Turkish support for the Syrian authorities.
On 4 February 2022, Fridays for Future activists demonstrated in Lysekil to draw attention to environmental problems and to demand action against climate change.

On 16 November 2020, union representatives of Workers Commissions (CCOO), General Union of Workers (UGT), Public Official's Independent Trade Union (CSIF), and Nursing Union (SATSE) protested in Palma de Mallorca (Balearic Islands) against the regional government's refusal of a salary increase for civil servants.
On 6 August 2022, more than 1,000 people marched as part of Pride in central Oulu, demonstrating for human and LGBT rights.

On 21 March 2022, on the International Day of Forests, employees of the Forestry Department, members of PASYDY, rallied outside the Ministry of Agriculture in Nicosia to protest over understaffing and the downgrading of education in their sector.

On 7 May 2023, around 200 people gathered in Ostseebad Binz (Mecklenburg-Vorpommern) to demonstrate against plans to build an LNG gas terminal in the city. Demonstrators argued the project would have a negative impact on the environment, and called for more climate protection.
On 29 June 2021, citizens protested in front of the health centre in Burela (Lugo), demanding a workforce increase. They also complained about of lack of technical resources.
On 30 November 2022, around 40 sixth-form college striking teachers represented by NEU picketed in Cambridge over below-inflation pay increases. Striking workers from UCU and CWU also joined them.

On 30 January 2020, an unknown number of farmers staged a protest action along the A1highway in Eembrugge (Utrecht) to put pressure on the negotiations between the Cabinet and the farmer organizations on 5 February.
On 10 January 2026, anti-immigration protesters gathered outside a hotel in Perth (Scotland) to demonstrate against the housing of asylum seekers in the hotel.

On 21 August 2023, anti-fascist demonstrators protested against the right-wing student organization called the Greater Dutch Student Association (GNSV: Groot-Nederlandse Studentenvereniging) at the Radboud University introduction market in Nijmegen (Gelderland). The protesters, holding a megaphone, chanted slogans like 'No fascism now, no fascism ever' to show their opposition to GNSV's presence at the university.

On 16 June 2020, in the morning, between 1,300 and 4,000 health workers gathered at the Charles de Gaulle esplanade in Rennes. They protested as part of the national day of actions for the defense of public hospitals.

On 30 May 2025, in the morning, at the call of several animal rights organizations, including Animal Rights and Animal Rebellion, around 35 people, including PvdD members, gathered in front of the provincial government building in Arnhem (Gelderland) to protest the decision by the province of Gelderland to permit the shooting of a wolf that had bitten a jogger in De Hoge Veluwe on 13 April 2025. Protesters chanted slogans, displayed signs and flags, and attempted to hand over a letter to the provincial authorities, demanding that the shooting permit be revoked, arguing that the decision was rushed, unjustified, and that people should learn to coexist with wolves.

On 9 February 2022, in the morning, representatives of 10 local environmental associations, including WWF, Fiab Napoli Cicloverdi, 'Green People' ('Gente Green') and NapoliBike, gathered, at the call of Legambiente, on the seaside promenade in Vittoria square in Napoli (Napoli, Campania) to protest against the Municipality's climate policies, specifically denouncing its alleged decision to allow cars on the seaside promenade during weekdays, citing increased pollution for residents.

On 18 November 2023, activists from Extinction Rebellion associated group held a sit-in protest in Linkoping, Ostergotland, to call for action against climate change and to raise awareness about environmental issues. The event was part of the Mothers' Rebellion global action held on November 18, 2023.

On 5 March 2020, Extinction Rebellion held a die-in protest at South Oxfordshire District Council in Milton Park, Oxford to protest against a housing plan which they claimed it would result in environmental destruction and too many homes.
On 1 June 2020, around 20 protesters gathered in Limerick city to support the Black Lives Matter movement and call for justice for George Floyd.

On 25 November 2024, on the occasion of the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, at the call of the municipality and the university, people took to the streets in Messina (Sicilia) to protest against gender violence. The carabinieri, the police, students, the mayor of Messina (civic list) and a councilor (no political affiliation reported) took part in the event.
On 9 July 2023, at the call of Sonneberg against the Right, several hundred people, including Antifa affiliates, demonstrated in Sonneberg against nationalism, racism and anti-Semitism.

On 5 December 2020, around 200 persons, including parents of students, gathered at Droits-de-L'Homme Square in Aurillac, at the call of FSU, SUD, CGT, PCF, LFI, MRAP, LDH, MFPF, and GJ. They denounced financial precariousness and called for the removal of article 24 of the 'comprehensive security' bill and denounced its potential infringement of the principle of freedom of information, especially on reporting on police brutality. The article criminalizes disseminating images with personal identifiers of a police or military officer, with the aim of affecting his or her physical or psychological integrity.

On 25 May 2024, about 2500 LGBTQ+ activists gathered for a pride march through Gdansk, demanding equal rights for people of all genders. Two counter-rallies were organized across the route, praising conservative values instead. No skirmishes were reported.

On 25 February 2022, Fridays for Future activists, led by Greta Thunberg, held a demonstration in front of the Parliament of Sweden in Stockholm to draw attention to environmental problems and to show support and solidarity with Ukraine and Ukrainians amid the ongoing Russian invasion.

On 25 January 2025, farmers with tractors staged a protest in Warwick (England) to demonstrate. The event was part of the National Day of Unity, a nationwide farmers' demonstration movement called by the NFU against proposed changes to agricultural inheritance tax (IHT). Before the protests, NFU president Tom Bradshaw and NFU Cymru president Aled Jones delivered a petition with over 270,000 public signatures to the Prime Minister's office, urging the government to abandon the plan.

On 30 October 2021, hundreds of people gathered in Trento e Trieste Square in Monza (Monza e della Brianza, Lombardia) to protest against the Senate's rejection of the 'Zan Law', a bill to criminalize violence and hate speech against LGBT people. PD, Possible, UdS, AGEDO, Rainbow Families, AI, and CGIL supported the demonstration.

On 28 June 2023, overnight, people rioted in Pontoise, vandalizing street furniture. A group of rioters threw mortar fireworks at the vehicle of the mayor of Pontoise, Stephanie Von Euw, while she was in it. The event was part of a national wave of riots and demonstrations denouncing police violence and demanding justice in the wake of the shooting and subsequent death of 17-year-old Nahel M. by a police officer in Nanterre on 27 June 2023.
On 19 February 2024, striking AlgoWatt workers demonstrated outside the town hall in Genova (Liguria) against their working conditions and delays in the payment of salaries.

On 7 November 2025, citizens and high-school students gathered in Kragujevac to support a hunger strike of a mother who lost her son following the collapse of the concrete canopy at the Novi Sad's railway station. She demands accountability for the tragedy, the release of detained students and snap elections. Protesters observed 16 minutes of silence to commemorate Novi Sad's victims. Earlier that day, high-school students decided to boycott their classes in support of the mother on hunger strike.
On 9 October 2022, around 250 people demonstrated in Berlin - Charlottenburg-Wilmersdorf for social justice. The call was made by the alliance 'Who has, who gives' and Quartiersmanagement Grunewald.

On 25 February 2023, Extinction Rebellion associated group demonstrated in Falun, Dalarna, calling on world leaders to take action to protect world oceans and to agree for a strong Global Ocean Treaty.
